3.42.d: तद् एतद् अमृतं गायत्रम् अथ यान्य् अन्यानि गीतानि काम्यान्य् एव तानि काम्यान्य् एव तानि । सप्तमे ऽनुवाके पञ्चमः खण्डः । सप्तमो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
3.42.e: That is the immortal gāyatra[-saman'\; and what other chants there are, they are optional only, they are optional only.
3.42.m:
Now this gāyatra chant is immortal. But whatever other songs there are, they are only for desired ends, they are only for desired ends.
[This is] the fifth subsection in the seventh section.
The seventh section is finished.

4.1.s: śvetāśvo darśato harinīlo 'si haritaspṛśas samānabuddho mā hiṃsīḥ na māṃ tvaṃ vettha pradrava |
4.1.d: श्वेताश्वो दर्शतो हरिनीलो ऽसि हरितस्पृशस् समानबुद्धो मा हिंसीः न मां त्वं वेत्थ प्रद्रव ।
4.1.e: Possessing white horses, conspicuous, yellow-blue art thou, do not harm. Thou knowest me not; run away.
4.1.m:
White horse, worthy of sight, dark-green-blue art thou, touching greenness; sharing one mind, do not injure [me]!
Thou dost not know me; run away!

4.1.s: yad abhyavacaraṇo 'bhyavaiṣi svapantam puruṣam akovidam aśmamayena varmaṇā varuṇo 'ntar dadhātu mā |
4.1.d: यद् अभ्यवचरणो ऽभ्यवैषि स्वपन्तम् पुरुषम् अकोविदम् अश्ममयेन वर्मणा वरुणो ऽन्तर् दधातु मा ।
4.1.e: When moving down against [him] thou descendest against the sleeping man unknowing, let Varuna cover me with a stone armor.
4.1.m:
When, descending, thou approachest the sleeping, inexperienced man,
let Varuṇa shield me with an armor made of stone!

4.1.s: yad abhyavacaraṇo 'bhyavaiṣi svapantam puruṣam akovidam ayasmayena varmaṇā varuṇo 'ntar dadhātu mā |
4.1.d: यद् अभ्यवचरणो ऽभ्यवैषि स्वपन्तम् पुरुषम् अकोविदम् अयस्मयेन वर्मणा वरुणो ऽन्तर् दधातु मा ।
4.1.e: When moving- down against [him] thou descendest against the sleeping man unknowing, let Varuna cover me with a brass armor.
4.1.m:
When, descending, thou approachest the sleeping, inexperienced man,
let Varuṇa shield me with an armor made of metal!

4.1.s: yad abhyavacaraṇo 'bhyavaiṣi svapantam puruṣam akovidaṃ lohamayena varmaṇā varuṇo 'ntar dadhātu mā |
4.1.d: यद् अभ्यवचरणो ऽभ्यवैषि स्वपन्तम् पुरुषम् अकोविदं लोहमयेन वर्मणा वरुणो ऽन्तर् दधातु मा ।
4.1.e: When moving down against [him] thou descendest against the sleeping man unknowing, let Varuna cover me with a copper armor.
4.1.m:
When, descending, thou approachest the sleeping, inexperienced man,
let Varuṇa shield me with an armor made of copper!

4.1.s: yad abhyavacaraṇo 'bhyavaiṣi svapantam puruṣam akovidaṃ rajatamayena varmaṇā varuṇo 'ntar dadhātu mā |
4.1.d: यद् अभ्यवचरणो ऽभ्यवैषि स्वपन्तम् पुरुषम् अकोविदं रजतमयेन वर्मणा वरुणो ऽन्तर् दधातु मा ।
4.1.e: When moving down against [him] thou descendest against the sleeping man unknowing, let Varuna cover me with a silver armor.
4.1.m:
When, descending, thou approachest the sleeping, inexperienced man,
let Varuṇa shield me with an armor made of silver!

4.1.s: yad abhyavacaraṇo 'bhyavaiṣi svapantam puruṣaṃ suvarṇamayena varmaṇā varuṇo 'ntar dadhātu mā |
4.1.d: यद् अभ्यवचरणो ऽभ्यवैषि स्वपन्तम् पुरुषं सुवर्णमयेन वर्मणा वरुणो ऽन्तर् दधातु मा ।
4.1.e: When moving down against [him] thou descendest against the sleeping man unknowing, let Varuna cover me with a golden armor.
4.1.m:
When, descending, thou approachest the sleeping, [inexperienced] man,
let Varuṇa shield me with an armor made of gold!

4.1.s: āyur mātā matiḥ pitā namas ta āviśoṣaṇa graho nāmāsi viśvāyus tasmai te viśvāhā namo namas tāmrāya namo varuṇāya namo jighāṃsate |
4.1.d: आयुर् माता मतिः पिता नमस् त आविशोषण ग्रहो नामासि विश्वायुस् तस्मै ते विश्वाहा नमो नमस् ताम्राय नमो वरुणाय नमो जिघांसते ।
4.1.e: Life is the mother, thought the father. Homage to thee, O drying one. Thou art seizer by name, possessing all life. TJnto thee then homage for ever. Homage to the copper-red one, homage to Varuna, homage to him who desires to slay.
4.1.m:
Life is mother, mind is father; homage to thee, O consumer!
Graha is thy name, of full life; to that thee, ever homage! Homage to the copper-colored! Homage to Varuṇa! Homage to him who desires to slay!

4.1.s: yakṣma rājan mā māṃ hiṃsīḥ rājan yakṣma mā hiṃsīḥ tayos saṃvidānayos sarvam āyur ayāny aham | prathamo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
4.1.d: यक्ष्म राजन् मा मां हिंसीः राजन् यक्ष्म मा हिंसीः तयोस् संविदानयोस् सर्वम् आयुर् अयान्य् अहम् । प्रथमो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
4.1.e: Consumption king, do not hurt me. King consumption, do not hurt. These two being harmonious, may I go to complete life.
4.1.m:
O King Consumption, do not injure me!
O King, do not injure [me], Consumption!
With those two agreeing together, may I attain a full life!
The first section is finished.

4.2.s: tasya yāni caturviṃśatir varṣāṇi tat prātassavanam caturviṃśatyakṣarā gāyatrī gāyatram prātassavanam |
4.2.d: तस्य यानि चतुर्विंशतिर् वर्षाणि तत् प्रातस्सवनम् चतुर्विंशत्यक्षरा गायत्री गायत्रम् प्रातस्सवनम् ।
4.2.e: His [first] twenty-four years are the morning-libation. The gdyatri has twenty-four syllables. The morning-libation is connected with the gdyatri.

4.2.s: tad vasūnām prāṇā vai vasavaḥ prāṇā hīdaṃ sarvaṃ vasv ādadate |
4.2.d: तद् वसूनाम् प्राणा वै वसवः प्राणा हीदं सर्वं वस्व् आददते ।
4.2.e: It belongs to the Vasus. The breaths are the Vasus; for the breaths take to themselves all this that is good (vasu).
4.2.m:
That belongs to the Vasus.
The vital breaths, indeed, are the Vasus,
for the vital breaths appropriate everything here as wealth.

4.2.s: sa yady enam etasmin kāla upatapad upadravet sa brūyāt prāṇā vasava idam me prātassavanam mādhyandinena savanenānusaṃtanuteti agado haiva bhavati |
4.2.d: स यद्य् एनम् एतस्मिन् काल उपतपद् उपद्रवेत् स ब्रूयात् प्राणा वसव इदम् मे प्रातस्सवनम् माध्यन्दिनेन सवनेनानुसंतनुतेति अगदो हैव भवति ।
4.2.e: If in that time an illness should attack him, he should say: " Ye breaths, ye Vasus, continue this morning-libation of mine by the noon-libation." Verily he becomes well.
4.2.m:
If disease should assail him at this time, he should say: 'O vital breaths, O Vasus, continue this morning pressing of mine to the midday pressing.'
He indeed becomes free from sickness.

4.2.s: atha yāni catuścatvāriṃśataṃ varṣāṇi tan mādhyandinaṃ savanam catuścatvāriṃśadakṣarā triṣṭup traiṣṭubham mādhyandinaṃ savanam |
4.2.d: अथ यानि चतुश्चत्वारिंशतं वर्षाणि तन् माध्यन्दिनं सवनम् चतुश्चत्वारिंशदक्षरा त्रिष्टुप् त्रैष्टुभम् माध्यन्दिनं सवनम् ।
4.2.e: His [next] forty-four years are the noon-libation. The tristubh has forty-four syllables. The noon-libation is connected with the tristubh.

4.2.s: tad rudrāṇām prāṇā vai rudrāḥ prāṇā hīdaṃ sarvaṃ rodayanti |
4.2.d: तद् रुद्राणाम् प्राणा वै रुद्राः प्राणा हीदं सर्वं रोदयन्ति ।
4.2.e: It belongs to the Rudras. The breaths are the Rudras; for the breaths cause the whole [universe] to wail {Śrud).
4.2.m:
That belongs to the Rudras.
The vital breaths, indeed, are the Rudras,
for the vital breaths make everything here weep.

4.2.s: sa yady enam etasmin kāla upatapad upadravet sa brūyāt prāṇā rudrā idam me mādhyandinaṃ savanaṃ tṛtīyasavanenānusaṃtanuteti agado haiva bhavati |
4.2.d: स यद्य् एनम् एतस्मिन् काल उपतपद् उपद्रवेत् स ब्रूयात् प्राणा रुद्रा इदम् मे माध्यन्दिनं सवनं तृतीयसवनेनानुसंतनुतेति अगदो हैव भवति ।
4.2.e: If in that time an illness should attack him, he should say: " Ye breaths, ye Rudras, continue this noon-libation of mine by the evening-libation." Verily he becomes well.
4.2.m:
If disease should assail him at this time, he should say: 'O vital breaths, O Rudras, continue this midday pressing of mine to the third pressing.'
He indeed becomes free from sickness.

4.2.s: atha yāny aṣṭācatvāriṃśataṃ varṣāṇi tat tṛtīyasavanam aṣṭācatvāriṃśadakṣarā jagatī jāgataṃ tṛtīyasavanam |
4.2.d: अथ यान्य् अष्टाचत्वारिंशतं वर्षाणि तत् तृतीयसवनम् अष्टाचत्वारिंशदक्षरा जगती जागतं तृतीयसवनम् ।
4.2.e: Moreover his [next] forty-eight years are the evening-libation. The jagati has forty-eight syllables. The evening-libation is connected with the jagati.
4.2.m: Now, the forty-eight years that follow are the third pressing. The jagatī [metre] has forty-eight syllables; the third pressing belongs to the jagatī.

4.2.s: tad ādityānām prāṇā vā ādityāḥ prāṇā hīdaṃ sarvam ādadate |
4.2.d: तद् आदित्यानाम् प्राणा वा आदित्याः प्राणा हीदं सर्वम् आददते ।
4.2.e: It belongs to the Adityas. The breaths are the Adityas; for the breaths take to themselves (,Śdd + d) this all.
4.2.m: That belongs to the Ādityas. The breaths indeed are the Ādityas, for the breaths take up (ādadate) all this.

4.2.s: sa yady enam etasmin kāla upatapad upadravet sa brūyāt prāṇā ādityā idam me tṛtīyasavanam āyuṣānusaṃtanuteti agado haiva bhavati |
4.2.d: स यद्य् एनम् एतस्मिन् काल उपतपद् उपद्रवेत् स ब्रूयात् प्राणा आदित्या इदम् मे तृतीयसवनम् आयुषानुसंतनुतेति अगदो हैव भवति ।
4.2.e: If in that time an illness should attack him, he should say: " Ye breaths, ye Adityas, continue this my evening-libation by my life-time." Verily he becomes well.
4.2.m: If illness should attack him during this period, let him say: 'O breaths, Ādityas, unite this third pressing of mine with life!' He indeed becomes free from disease.

4.2.s: etad dha tad vidvān brāhmaṇa uvāca mahidāsa aitareya upatapati kim idam upatapasi yo 'ham anenopatapatā na preṣyāmīti sa ha ṣoḍaśaśataṃ varṣāṇi jijīva pra ha ṣoḍaśaśataṃ varṣāṇi jīvati nainam prāṇas sāmy āyuṣo jahāti ya evaṃ veda | dvitīyo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
4.2.d: एतद् ध तद् विद्वान् ब्राह्मण उवाच महिदास ऐतरेय उपतपति किम् इदम् उपतपसि यो ऽहम् अनेनोपतपता न प्रेष्यामीति स ह षोडशशतं वर्षाणि जिजीव प्र ह षोडशशतं वर्षाणि जीवति नैनम् प्राणस् साम्य् आयुषो जहाति य एवं वेद । द्वितीयो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
4.2.e: Now the Brahman Mahidasa Aitareya, knowing this, said in [his] illness: " Why dost thou now attack me, who am not to die of this illness?" He lived a hundred and sixteen years. He lives on to a hundred and sixteen years, [his] breath does not leave him in the midst of his lifetime, who knows thus.
4.2.m:
Knowing this, the brāhmaṇa Mahidāsa Aitareya said when he fell ill: 'Why do you plague me with this illness, when I shall not die of it?' He lived for a hundred and sixteen years. Indeed, he who knows this lives for a hundred and sixteen years; the breath does not leave him midway through his life.
The second anuvāka is completed.

4.3.s: tryāyuṣaṃ kaśyapasya jamadagnes tryāyuṣam trīṇy amṛtasya puṣpāṇi trīṇy āyūṃṣi me 'kṛṇoḥ |
4.3.d: त्र्यायुषं कश्यपस्य जमदग्नेस् त्र्यायुषम् त्रीण्य् अमृतस्य पुष्पाणि त्रीण्य् आयूंषि मे ऽकृणोः ।
4.3.e: The threefold life-time of Ka5yapa, of Jamadagni the threefold life-time, the three flowers of immortality, three life-times thou madest for me.
4.3.m: 'A triple lifespan of Kaśyapa, a triple lifespan of Jamadagni, / three flowers of immortality: you have made three lifespans for me.

4.3.s: sa no mayobhūḥ pitav āviśasva śāntiko yas tanuve syonaḥ |
4.3.d: स नो मयोभूः पितव् आविशस्व शान्तिको यस् तनुवे स्योनः ।
4.3.e: Enter into us, O thou beneficent food, which, tranquilizing, art pleasing to the body.
4.3.m: O food, enter us as our joy, bringing peace, pleasant to the body.

4.3.s: ye 'gnayaḥ purīṣyāḥ praviṣṭāḥ pṛṭhivīm anu teṣāṃ tvam asy uttamaḥ pra ṇo jīvātave suva | tṛtīyo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
4.3.d: ये ऽग्नयः पुरीष्याः प्रविष्टाः पृठिवीम् अनु तेषां त्वम् अस्य् उत्तमः प्र णो जीवातवे सुव । तृतीयो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
4.3.e: What dirty fires are entered into the earth along, of them thou art the highest; impel us unto life.
4.3.m:
Those fires that are rich in soil, entered along the earth, / among them you are the highest: impel us toward life.'
The third anuvāka is completed.

4.4.s: araṇyasya vatso 'si viśvanāmā viśvābhirakṣaṇo 'pām pakvo 'si varuṇasya dūto 'ntardhināma |
4.4.d: अरण्यस्य वत्सो ऽसि विश्वनामा विश्वाभिरक्षणो ऽपाम् पक्वो ऽसि वरुणस्य दूतो ऽन्तर्धिनाम ।
4.4.e: Thou art the calf of the forest, possessing all names, all-defending; ripe of the waters art thou, Varuna's messenger, concealment by name.
4.4.m: You are the calf of the wilderness, all-named, all-protecting, the ripened product of the waters, the messenger of Varuṇa, your name is concealment.

4.4.s: yathā tvam amṛto martyebhyo 'ntarhito 'sy evaṃ tvam asmān aghāyubhyo 'ntar dhehi antardhir asi stenebhyaḥ | caturtho 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
4.4.d: यथा त्वम् अमृतो मर्त्येभ्यो ऽन्तर्हितो ऽस्य् एवं त्वम् अस्मान् अघायुभ्यो ऽन्तर् धेहि अन्तर्धिर् असि स्तेनेभ्यः । चतुर्थो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
4.4.e: As thou, immortal, art concealed from mortals, so do thou conceal us from the wicked. Thou art concealment from robbers.
4.4.m:
Just as you, being immortal, are concealed from mortals, so conceal us from the malicious. You are a concealment against thieves.
The fourth anuvāka is completed.

4.5.s: vyuṣi savitā bhavasy udeṣyan viṣṇur udyan puruṣa udito bṛhaspatir abhiprayan maghavendro vaikuṇṭho mādhyandine bhago 'parāhna ugro devo lohitāyann astamite yamo bhavasi |
4.5.d: व्युषि सविता भवस्य् उदेष्यन् विष्णुर् उद्यन् पुरुष उदितो बृहस्पतिर् अभिप्रयन् मघवेन्द्रो वैकुण्ठो माध्यन्दिने भगो ऽपराह्न उग्रो देवो लोहितायन्न् अस्तमिते यमो भवसि ।
4.5.e: When it dawns, thou becomest Savitar; when about to rise, Visnu; rising, Purusa; risen, Brhaspati; ascending, the bounteous one; at noon, Indra Vfiikuntha; in the afternoon, Bhaga; growing red, the formidable god; having set, thou becomest Yama.
4.5.m: At dawn you become Savitṛ; about to rise, Viṣṇu; rising, Puruṣa; risen, Bṛhaspati; marching forth, Indra Maghavat Vaikuṇṭha; at midday, Bhaga; in the afternoon, Ugra Deva; turning red, [Rudra]; set, you become Yama.

4.5.s: aśnasu somo rājā niśāyām pitṛrājas svapne manuṣyān praviśasi payasā paśūn |
4.5.d: अश्नसु सोमो राजा निशायाम् पितृराजस् स्वप्ने मनुष्यान् प्रविशसि पयसा पशून् ।
4.5.e: In the stones king Soma, in the night the king of the Fathers. In sleep thou enterest into men; with the milk, into cattle.
4.5.m: Among food-eaters [you are] King Soma; in the night, the king of the ancestors; in sleep you enter human beings; with milk, the cattle.

4.5.s: virātre bhavo bhavasy apararātre 'ṅgirā agnihotravelāyām bhṛguḥ |
4.5.d: विरात्रे भवो भवस्य् अपररात्रे ऽङ्गिरा अग्निहोत्रवेलायाम् भृगुः ।
4.5.e: In the middle of night thou art Bhava; in the after-part of the night, Angiras; at the time of the Agnihotra, Bhrgu.
4.5.m: In the deep of the night you become Bhava; in the latter part of the night, Aṅgiras; at the time of the agnihotra, Bhṛgu.

4.5.s: tasya tad etad eva maṇḍalam ūdhaḥ tasyaitau stanau yad vāk ca prāṇaś ca tābhyām me dhukṣvādhyāyam brahmacaryam prajām paśūn svargaṃ lokaṃ sajātavanasyām |
4.5.d: तस्य तद् एतद् एव मण्डलम् ऊधः तस्यैतौ स्तनौ यद् वाक् च प्राणश् च ताभ्याम् मे धुक्ष्वाध्यायम् ब्रह्मचर्यम् प्रजाम् पशून् स्वर्गं लोकं सजातवनस्याम् ।
4.5.e: This disk is its udder, speech and breath are these two teats. From them milk for me the lesson, Vedic studentship, oifspring, domestic animals, the heavenly world, the prayer for supremacy over [my] fellows,
4.5.m: This very orb of his is the udder. Its two teats are speech and breath. From them milk out for me Vedic study, celibacy, offspring, cattle, the heavenly world, and dominance over my kinsmen.

4.5.s: etā āśiṣa āśāse bhūr bhuvas svaḥ udite śukram ādiśa tad atman dadhe | pañcamo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
4.5.d: एता आशिष आशासे भूर् भुवस् स्वः उदिते शुक्रम् आदिश तद् अत्मन् दधे । पञ्चमो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
4.5.e: These wishes I wish. Hhus, bhuvas, svar. When [the sun] hath risen, show brightness. I place that in [my]self.
4.5.m:
These blessings I pray for: bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, svaḥ! When [the sun] has risen, point to its brightness: 'That I place in myself.'
The fifth anuvāka is completed.

4.6.s: bhageratho haikṣvāko rājā kāmapreṇa yajñena yakṣyamāṇa āsa |
4.6.d: भगेरथो हैक्ष्वाको राजा कामप्रेण यज्ञेन यक्ष्यमाण आस ।
4.6.e: King Bhageratha Aiksvaka was about to sacrifice with a wish-fulfilling sacrifice.
4.6.m: Bhageratha, an Aikṣvāka king, was about to sacrifice with a sacrifice that grants all desires.

4.6.s: tad u ha kurupañcālānām brāhmaṇā ūcur bhageratho ha vā ayam aikṣvāko rājā kāmapreṇa yajñena yakṣyamāṇaḥ etena kathāṃ vadiṣyāma iti |
4.6.d: तद् उ ह कुरुपञ्चालानाम् ब्राह्मणा ऊचुर् भगेरथो ह वा अयम् ऐक्ष्वाको राजा कामप्रेण यज्ञेन यक्ष्यमाणः एतेन कथां वदिष्याम इति ।
4.6.e: Then the Brahmans of the Kurupaficalas said: "Verily this king Bhageratha Aiksvaka is about to sacrifice with a wish-fulfilling sacrifice. With him we will have a talk."
4.6.m: Then the brāhmaṇas of the Kuru-Pañcālas said: 'This King Bhageratha Aikṣvāka is about to sacrifice with a sacrifice that grants all desires. Let us engage in a discussion with him.'

4.6.d: तं हाभ्येयुः तेभ्यो हाभ्यागतेभ्यो ऽपचितीश् चकार ।
4.6.e: They went to him. To them having come to [him] he paid honors.
4.6.m: They approached him. He showed honor to them when they had arrived.

4.6.s: atha haiṣāṃ sa bhāga āvavrājoptvā keśaśmaśrūṇi nakhān nikṛtyājyenābhyajya daṇḍopānaham bibhrat |
4.6.d: अथ हैषां स भाग आवव्राजोप्त्वा केशश्मश्रूणि नखान् निकृत्याज्येनाभ्यज्य दण्डोपानहम् बिभ्रत् ।
4.6.e: Now he came to their place having cut the hair of his head and his beard, having cut his nails, having anointed himself with sacrificial batter, bearing a staff and sandals.
4.6.m: Then that [king] went to their portion, having shaved his hair and beard, clipped his nails, anointed himself with clarified butter, and holding a staff and sandals.

4.6.s: tān hovāca brāhmaṇā bhagavantaḥ katamo vas tad veda yathāśrāvitapratyāśrāvite devān gacchata iti |
4.6.d: तान् होवाच ब्राह्मणा भगवन्तः कतमो वस् तद् वेद यथाश्रावितप्रत्याश्राविते देवान् गच्छत इति ।
4.6.e: To them he (Bhageratha) said: " Reverend Brahmans, who of you knoweth this: how address and response go to the gods?"
4.6.m: He said to them: 'Reverend brāhmaṇas, which of you knows how the call and the response reach the gods?'

4.6.s: atha hovāca katamo vas tad veda yadviduṣas sūdgātā suhotā svadhvaryus sumānuṣavid ājāyata iti |
4.6.d: अथ होवाच कतमो वस् तद् वेद यद्विदुषस् सूद्गाता सुहोता स्वध्वर्युस् सुमानुषविद् आजायत इति ।
4.6.e: Then he said: " Who of you knoweth what he knoweth (= must know) of whom, a good udgdtar, a good hotar, a good acthvaryu, one who knoweth men well, is born?"
4.6.m: Then he said: 'Which of you knows by knowing what one becomes a good udgātṛ, a good hotṛ, a good adhvaryu, and a knower of human nature?'

4.6.s: atha hovāca katamo vas tad veda yac chandāṃsi prayujyante yat tāni sarvāṇi saṃstutāny abhisampadyanta iti |
4.6.d: अथ होवाच कतमो वस् तद् वेद यच् छन्दांसि प्रयुज्यन्ते यत् तानि सर्वाणि संस्तुतान्य् अभिसम्पद्यन्त इति ।
4.6.e: Then he said: " Who of you knoweth this: how the metres are applied, to what all of them when used in praise together are equivalent?"
4.6.m: Then he said: 'Which of you knows that when metres are employed, into what all of them merge when chanted together?'

4.6.s: atha hovāca katamo vas tad veda yathā gāyatryā uttame akṣare punar yajñam apigacchata iti |
4.6.d: अथ होवाच कतमो वस् तद् वेद यथा गायत्र्या उत्तमे अक्षरे पुनर् यज्ञम् अपिगच्छत इति ।
4.6.e: Then he said: " Who of you knoweth this: how the last two syllables of the gāyatrī go again unto the sacrifice?"
4.6.m: Then he said: 'Which of you knows how the two final syllables of the gāyatrī reach the sacrifice again?'

4.6.s: atha hovāca katamo vas tad veda yathā dakṣiṇāḥ pratigṛhītā na hiṃsantīti | ṣaṣṭhe 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
4.6.d: अथ होवाच कतमो वस् तद् वेद यथा दक्षिणाः प्रतिगृहीता न हिंसन्तीति । षष्ठे ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
4.6.e: Then he said: " Who of you knoweth this: how the sacrificial fees, being received, do not injure?"
4.6.m:
Then he said: 'Which of you knows how priestly gifts, when accepted, do not injure?'
First subsection in the sixth anuvāka.

4.7.e: These five questions he asked of them.
4.7.m: These were the five questions he asked them.

4.7.s: teṣāṃ ha kurupañcālānām bako dālbhyo 'nūcāna āsa |
4.7.d: तेषां ह कुरुपञ्चालानाम् बको दाल्भ्यो ऽनूचान आस ।
4.7.e: Of these Kurupaficalas Baka Dalbhya was learned.
4.7.m: Among those Kuru-Pañcālas, Baka Dālbhya was learned in the Veda.

4.7.s: sa hovāca yathāśrāvitapratyāśrāvite devān gacchata iti prācyāṃ vai rājan diśy āśrāvitapratyāśrāvite devān gacchataḥ tasmāt prāṅ tiṣṭhann āśrāvayati prāṅ tiṣṭhan pratyāśrāvayatīti |
4.7.d: स होवाच यथाश्रावितप्रत्याश्राविते देवान् गच्छत इति प्राच्यां वै राजन् दिश्य् आश्रावितप्रत्याश्राविते देवान् गच्छतः तस्मात् प्राङ् तिष्ठन्न् आश्रावयति प्राङ् तिष्ठन् प्रत्याश्रावयतीति ।
4.7.e: He said: "' How address and response go to the gods?'—verily in the eastern quarter, O king, do address and response go to the gods. Therefore standing towards the east one maketh address, [and] standing towards the east one maketh response."
4.7.m: He said: '[Regarding your question,] how the call and the response reach the gods: in the eastern quarter, O king, the call and the response reach the gods. Therefore, standing facing east, one makes the call; standing facing east, one makes the response.'

4.7.s: atha hovāca yadviduṣas sūdgātā suhotā svadhvaryus sumānuṣavid ājāyata iti yo vai manuṣyasya sambhūtiṃ vedeti hovāca tasya sūdgātā suhotā svadhvaryus sumānuṣavid ājāyata iti prāṇā u ha vāva rājan manuṣyasya sambhūtir eveti |
4.7.d: अथ होवाच यद्विदुषस् सूद्गाता सुहोता स्वध्वर्युस् सुमानुषविद् आजायत इति यो वै मनुष्यस्य सम्भूतिं वेदेति होवाच तस्य सूद्गाता सुहोता स्वध्वर्युस् सुमानुषविद् आजायत इति प्राणा उ ह वाव राजन् मनुष्यस्य सम्भूतिर् एवेति ।
4.7.e: Then he said: " 'What he knoweth (=must know) of whom a good udgdtar, a good hotar, a good adhvaryu, one who knoweth men well, is born?'—verily he who knoweth the origination of man," he said, " of him a good udgdtar, a good hotar, a good adhvaryu, one who knoweth men well, is born. And the breaths, indeed, O king, are the origination of man."
4.7.m: Then he said: '[Regarding your question,] by knowing what one becomes a good udgātṛ, a good hotṛ, a good adhvaryu, and a knower of human nature: he who knows the origination of man—he said—becomes a good udgātṛ, a good hotṛ, a good adhvaryu, and a knower of human nature. The breaths indeed, O king, are the origination of man.'

4.7.s: atha hovāca yac chandāṃsi prayujyante yat tāni sarvāṇi saṃstutāny abhisampadyanta iti gāyatrīm u ha vāva rājan sarvāṇi chandāṃsi saṃstutāny abhisampadyanta iti |
4.7.d: अथ होवाच यच् छन्दांसि प्रयुज्यन्ते यत् तानि सर्वाणि संस्तुतान्य् अभिसम्पद्यन्त इति गायत्रीम् उ ह वाव राजन् सर्वाणि छन्दांसि संस्तुतान्य् अभिसम्पद्यन्त इति ।
4.7.e: Then he said: "' How the metres are applied, to what all of them when used in praise together are equivalent?'—verily to the gāyatrī, O king, all the metres when used in praise together are equivalent."
4.7.m: Then he said: '[Regarding your question,] when metres are employed, into what all of them merge when chanted together: into the gāyatrī indeed, O king, all metres merge when chanted together.'

4.7.s: atha hovāca yathā gāyatryā uttame akṣare punar yajñam apigacchata iti vaṣaṭkāreṇo ha vāva rājan gāyatryā uttame akṣare punar yajñam apigacchata iti |
4.7.d: अथ होवाच यथा गायत्र्या उत्तमे अक्षरे पुनर् यज्ञम् अपिगच्छत इति वषट्कारेणो ह वाव राजन् गायत्र्या उत्तमे अक्षरे पुनर् यज्ञम् अपिगच्छत इति ।
4.7.e: Then he said: "' How the last two syllables of the gāyatrī go again unto the sacrifice?'—verily by means of the vasatkdra, O king, the two last syllables of the gāyatrī go again unto the sacrifice."
4.7.m: Then he said: '[Regarding your question,] how the two final syllables of the gāyatrī reach the sacrifice again: by means of the vaṣaṭ-call indeed, O king, the two final syllables of the gāyatrī reach the sacrifice again.'

4.7.s: atha hovāca yathā dakṣiṇāḥ pratigṛhītā na hiṃsantīti | ṣaṣṭhe 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
4.7.d: अथ होवाच यथा दक्षिणाः प्रतिगृहीता न हिंसन्तीति । षष्ठे ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः ।
4.7.e: Then he said: "' How the sacrificial fees, being received, do not injure?'—
4.7.m:
Then he said: '[Regarding your question,] how priestly gifts, when accepted, do not injure:'
Second subsection in the sixth anuvāka.

4.8.s: yo vai gāyatryai mukhaṃ vedeti hovāca taṃ dakṣiṇā pratigṛhītā na hiṃsantīti |
4.8.d: यो वै गायत्र्यै मुखं वेदेति होवाच तं दक्षिणा प्रतिगृहीता न हिंसन्तीति ।
4.8.e: — Verily whoso knoweth the mouth of the gāyatrī," he said, "him the sacrificial fees, being received, do not injure.
4.8.m: 'He who knows the mouth of the gāyatrī,' he said, 'him priestly gifts do not injure when accepted.'

4.8.s: agnir ha vāva rājan gāyatrīmukham tasmād yad agnāv abhyādadhāti bhūyān eva sa tena bhavati vardhate evam evaivaṃ vidvān brāhmaṇaḥ pratigṛhṇan bhūyān eva bhavati vardhata u eveti |
4.8.d: अग्निर् ह वाव राजन् गायत्रीमुखम् तस्माद् यद् अग्नाव् अभ्यादधाति भूयान् एव स तेन भवति वर्धते एवम् एवैवं विद्वान् ब्राह्मणः प्रतिगृह्णन् भूयान् एव भवति वर्धत उ एवेति ।
4.8.e: Verily Agni, O king, is the mouth of the gāyatrī. Therefore in that one puts [things] in the fire, it thereby becometh greater, it increaseth; even so a Brahman knowing thus, receiving [sacrificial fees], becometh greater [and] increaseth."
4.8.m: 'Agni indeed, O king, is the mouth of the gāyatrī. Therefore, whatever one puts into Agni, he becomes greater by that, he increases. In the very same way, the brāhmaṇa who knows this, upon accepting [gifts], becomes greater and increases.'

4.8.s: sa hovācānūcāno vai kilāyam brāhmaṇa āsa tvām aham anena yajñenaimīti |
4.8.d: स होवाचानूचानो वै किलायम् ब्राह्मण आस त्वाम् अहम् अनेन यज्ञेनैमीति ।
4.8.e: He (Bhageratha) said: " Verily this one was a learned Brahman. I come to thee with this sacrifice."
4.8.m: He [the king] said: 'This brāhmaṇa is indeed truly learned in the Veda! I approach you for this sacrifice.'

4.8.s: tasya vai te tathodgāsyāmīti hovāca yathaikarāḍ eva bhūtvā svargaṃ lokam eṣyasīti |
4.8.d: तस्य वै ते तथोद्गास्यामीति होवाच यथैकराड् एव भूत्वा स्वर्गं लोकम् एष्यसीति ।
4.8.e: " Verily, I will sing for thee its udgītha," he (B.) said, " in such wise that thou shalt go to the heavenly world having become sole king."
4.8.m: 'Indeed, I shall chant the udgītha for you in such a way,' he said, 'that having become a sole ruler, you will go to the heavenly world.'

4.8.s: tasmā etena gāyatreṇodgīthenojjagau sa haikarāḍ eva bhūtvā svargaṃ lokam iyāya tena haitenaikarāḍ eva bhūtvā svargaṃ lokam eti |
4.8.d: तस्मा एतेन गायत्रेणोद्गीथेनोज्जगौ स हैकराड् एव भूत्वा स्वर्गं लोकम् इयाय तेन हैतेनैकराड् एव भूत्वा स्वर्गं लोकम् एति ।
4.8.e: For him he sang the udgītha by means of the gāyatra-udgītha. He (Bhageratha) having become sole king went to the heavenly world. By means of this same \udgītha\ he goes to the heavenly world, having become sole king, [who knows thus].
4.8.m: He chanted the udgītha for him with this gāyatra chant. Having become a sole ruler, he went to the heavenly world. Through this chant, having become a sole ruler, he who knows this goes to the heavenly world.

4.8.s: oṃ vā iti dve akṣare oṃ vā iti caturthe oṃ vā iti ṣaṣṭhe hum bhā oṃ vāg ity aṣṭame |
4.8.d: ओं वा इति द्वे अक्षरे ओं वा इति चतुर्थे ओं वा इति षष्ठे हुम् भा ओं वाग् इत्य् अष्टमे ।
4.8.e: Om vd are two syllables, om. vd the third and fourth, om vd the fifth and sixth, hum bhd, om, vdc the seventh and eighth.
4.8.m: 'om vāc' are two syllables; 'om vāc' at the fourth; 'om vāc' at the sixth; 'hum bhā om vāk' at the eighth.

4.8.e: With thjs same [udglthal Pratidar§a sang the udgītha for this Bhayada Asamatya.
4.8.m: With this [udgītha], Pratīdarśa chanted for Bhayada Āsamātyasa.

4.8.s: taṃ hovāca kiṃ ta āgāsyāmīti sa hovāca harī me devāśvāv āgāyeti tatheti tau hāsmā ājagau tau hainam ājagmatuḥ |
4.8.d: तं होवाच किं त आगास्यामीति स होवाच हरी मे देवाश्वाव् आगायेति तथेति तौ हास्मा आजगौ तौ हैनम् आजग्मतुः ।
4.8.e: He said to him: " What shall I sing into thy possession?" He said: "Sing for me the two bay steeds of the gods." "Yes," he said. He sang the two into his possession. They both came unto him.
4.8.m: He said to him: 'What shall I chant for you?' He said: 'Chant into being for me two bay divine horses.' 'So be it,' [he replied]. He chanted them into being for him. The two came to him.

4.8.s: sa vā eṣa udgīthaḥ kāmānāṃ sampad oṃ vā3c oṃ vā3c oṃ vā3c hum bhā oṃ vāg iti sāṅgo haiva satanur amṛtas sambhavati ya etad evaṃ vedātho yasyaivaṃ vidvān udgāyati | ṣaṣṭhe 'nuvāke tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ | ṣaṣṭho 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
4.8.d: स वा एष उद्गीथः कामानां सम्पद् ओं वा3च् ओं वा3च् ओं वा3च् हुम् भा ओं वाग् इति साङ्गो हैव सतनुर् अमृतस् सम्भवति य एतद् एवं वेदाथो यस्यैवं विद्वान् उद्गायति । षष्ठे ऽनुवाके तृतीयः खण्डः । षष्ठो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
4.8.e: This same udgītha is the success of wishes, viz. om, vdc, om vdc, om vdc, hum bhd, om vdc. Verily he comes to life with limbs, with a body, immortal, who knows this thus, and he for whom one knowing thus sings the udgītha.
4.8.m:
This udgītha is the attainment of all desires: 'om vāc, om vāc, om vāc, hum bhā om vāk.' Complete with limbs, with a body, he is born immortal who knows this thus, and also he for whom one who knows this chants the udgītha.
Third subsection in the sixth anuvāka.
The sixth anuvāka is completed.

4.9.s: puruṣo vai yajñaḥ puruṣo hodgīthaḥ athaita eva mṛtyavo yad agnir vāyur ādityaś candramāḥ |
4.9.d: पुरुषो वै यज्ञः पुरुषो होद्गीथः अथैत एव मृत्यवो यद् अग्निर् वायुर् आदित्यश् चन्द्रमाः ।
4.9.e: Verily the sacrifice is man, the udgītha indeed is man. Now these are the deaths, viz. Agni, Vayu, the sun, the moon.
4.9.m: The sacrifice is indeed the Puruṣa; the udgītha is indeed the Puruṣa. Now these are deaths: Agni, Vāyu, Āditya, and the Moon.

4.9.s: te ha puruṣaṃ jāyamānam eva mṛtyupāśair abhidadhati tasya vācam evāgnir abhidadhāti prāṇaṃ vāyuś cakṣur ādityaś śrotraṃ candramāḥ |
4.9.d: ते ह पुरुषं जायमानम् एव मृत्युपाशैर् अभिदधति तस्य वाचम् एवाग्निर् अभिदधाति प्राणं वायुश् चक्षुर् आदित्यश् श्रोत्रं चन्द्रमाः ।
4.9.e: They put upon man, when he is being born, the fetters of death. Agni puts [them] upon his speech, Vayu upon his breath, the sun upon his sight, the moon upon his hearing,
4.9.m:
They indeed bind the man right as he is born with the nooses of death.
Agni binds his speech, Vāyu his breath, Āditya his sight, the Moon his hearing.

4.9.s: tad āhus sa vā udgātā yo yajamānasya prāṇebhyo 'dhi mṛtyupāśān unmuñcatīti |
4.9.d: तद् आहुस् स वा उद्गाता यो यजमानस्य प्राणेभ्यो ऽधि मृत्युपाशान् उन्मुञ्चतीति ।
4.9.e: This they say: " Verily it is the udgdtar who releaseth the fetters of death from the breaths of the sacrificer."
4.9.m: Regarding this they say: 'He indeed is an udgātṛ who releases the nooses of death from the sacrificer's vital breaths.'

4.9.s: tad yasyaivaṃ vidvān prastauti ya evāsya vāci mṛtyupāśas tam evāsyonmuñcati |
4.9.d: तद् यस्यैवं विद्वान् प्रस्तौति य एवास्य वाचि मृत्युपाशस् तम् एवास्योन्मुञ्चति ।
4.9.e: For whom one knowing thus sings the prastāva, for him he releases that fetter of death which is in his speech.
4.9.m: Therefore, for whom one knowing thus chants the prastāva, whatever noose of death is in his speech, that he releases from him.

4.9.s: atha yasyaivaṃ vidvān udgāyati ya evāsya prāṇe mṛtyupāśas tam evāsyonmuñcati |
4.9.d: अथ यस्यैवं विद्वान् उद्गायति य एवास्य प्राणे मृत्युपाशस् तम् एवास्योन्मुञ्चति ।
4.9.e: And for whom one knowing thus sings the udgītha, for him he releases that fetter of death which is in his breath,
4.9.m: Then, for whom one knowing thus chants the udgītha, whatever noose of death is in his breath, that he releases from him.

4.9.s: atha yasyaivaṃ vidvān pratiharati ya evāsya cakṣuṣi mṛtyupāśas tam evāsyonmuñcati |
4.9.d: अथ यस्यैवं विद्वान् प्रतिहरति य एवास्य चक्षुषि मृत्युपाशस् तम् एवास्योन्मुञ्चति ।
4.9.e: And for whom one knowing thus sings the pratihāra, for him he releases that fetter of death which is in his sight.
4.9.m: Then, for whom one knowing thus chants the pratihāra, whatever noose of death is in his sight, that he releases from him.

4.9.s: atha yasyaivaṃ vidvān nidhanam upaiti ya evāsya śrotre mṛtyupāśas tam evāsyonmuñcati |
4.9.d: अथ यस्यैवं विद्वान् निधनम् उपैति य एवास्य श्रोत्रे मृत्युपाशस् तम् एवास्योन्मुञ्चति ।
4.9.e: And for whom one knowing thus enters upon the nidhana, for him he releases that fetter of death which is in his hearing.
4.9.m: Then, for whom one knowing thus reaches the nidhana, whatever noose of death is in his hearing, that he releases from him.

4.9.s: evaṃ vā evaṃvid udgātā yajamānasya prāṇebhyo 'dhi mṛtyupāśān unmuñcati |
4.9.d: एवं वा एवंविद् उद्गाता यजमानस्य प्राणेभ्यो ऽधि मृत्युपाशान् उन्मुञ्चति ।
4.9.e: Thus an udgdtar knowing thus releases the fetters of death from the breaths of the sacrificer.
4.9.m: Thus indeed the udgātṛ who knows thus releases the nooses of death from the sacrificer's vital breaths.

4.9.s: tad āhus sa vā udgātā yo yajamānasya prāṇebhyo 'dhi mṛtyupāśān unmucyāthainaṃ sāṅgaṃ satanuṃ sarvamṛtyos spṛṇātīti | saptame 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
4.9.d: तद् आहुस् स वा उद्गाता यो यजमानस्य प्राणेभ्यो ऽधि मृत्युपाशान् उन्मुच्याथैनं साङ्गं सतनुं सर्वमृत्योस् स्पृणातीति । सप्तमे ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
4.9.e: This they say: " He is an udgdtar who, having released the fetters of death from the breaths of the sacrificer, rescueth him then with his limbs, with his body, from every death."
4.9.m:
Regarding this they say: 'He indeed is an udgātṛ who, having released the nooses of death from the sacrificer's vital breaths, then rescues him, with all his limbs and with his body, from all death.'
First khaṇḍa in the seventh anuvāka.

4.10.s: tad yasyaivaṃ vidvān hiṅkaroti ya evāsya lomasu mṛtyupāśas tasmād evainaṃ spṛṇāti |
4.10.d: तद् यस्यैवं विद्वान् हिङ्करोति य एवास्य लोमसु मृत्युपाशस् तस्माद् एवैनं स्पृणाति ।
4.10.e: Now for whom one knowing thus utters the hinkdra, him he rescues from that fetter of death which is in his hairs.
4.10.m: Therefore, for whom one knowing thus makes the hiṅkāra, from whatever noose of death is in his body hairs, from that he rescues him.

4.10.s: atha yasyaivaṃ vidvān prastauti ya evāsya tvaci mṛtyupāśas tasmād evainaṃ spṛṇāti |
4.10.d: अथ यस्यैवं विद्वान् प्रस्तौति य एवास्य त्वचि मृत्युपाशस् तस्माद् एवैनं स्पृणाति ।
4.10.e: And for whom one knowing thus sings the prastāva, him he rescues from that fetter of death which is in his skin.
4.10.m: Then, for whom one knowing thus chants the prastāva, from whatever noose of death is in his skin, from that he rescues him.

4.10.s: atha yasyaivaṃ vidvān ādim ādatte ya evāsya māṃseṣu mṛtyupāśas tasmād evainaṃ spṛṇāti |
4.10.d: अथ यस्यैवं विद्वान् आदिम् आदत्ते य एवास्य मांसेषु मृत्युपाशस् तस्माद् एवैनं स्पृणाति ।
4.10.e: And for whom one knowing thus begins the ddi, him he rescues from that fetter of death which is in his flesh.
4.10.m: Then, for whom one knowing thus takes up the ādi, from whatever noose of death is in his flesh, from that he rescues him.

4.10.s: atha yasyaivaṃ vidvān udgāyati ya evāsya snāvasu mṛtyupāśas tasmād evainaṃ spṛṇāti |
4.10.d: अथ यस्यैवं विद्वान् उद्गायति य एवास्य स्नावसु मृत्युपाशस् तस्माद् एवैनं स्पृणाति ।
4.10.e: And for whom one knowing thus sings the udgitha, him he rescues from that fetter of death which is in his sinews,
4.10.m: Then, for whom one knowing thus chants the udgītha, from whatever noose of death is in his sinews, from that he rescues him.

4.10.s: atha yasyaivaṃ vidvān pratiharati ya evāsyāṅgeṣu mṛtyupāśas tasmād evainaṃ spṛṇāti |
4.10.d: अथ यस्यैवं विद्वान् प्रतिहरति य एवास्याङ्गेषु मृत्युपाशस् तस्माद् एवैनं स्पृणाति ।
4.10.e: And for whom one knowing thus sings the pratihāra, him he rescues from that fetter of death which is in his limbs.
4.10.m: Then, for whom one knowing thus chants the pratihāra, from whatever noose of death is in his limbs, from that he rescues him.

4.10.s: atha yasyaivaṃ vidvān upadravati ya evāsyāsthiṣu mṛtyupāśas tasmād evainaṃ spṛṇāti |
4.10.d: अथ यस्यैवं विद्वान् उपद्रवति य एवास्यास्थिषु मृत्युपाशस् तस्माद् एवैनं स्पृणाति ।
4.10.e: And for whom one knowing thus sings the vpadrava, him he rescues from that fetter of death which is in his bones.
4.10.m: Then, for whom one knowing thus chants the upadrava, from whatever noose of death is in his bones, from that he rescues him.

4.10.s: atha yasyaivaṃ vidvān nidhanam upaiti ya evāsya majjasu mṛtyupāśas sa tasmād evainaṃ spṛṇāti |
4.10.d: अथ यस्यैवं विद्वान् निधनम् उपैति य एवास्य मज्जसु मृत्युपाशस् स तस्माद् एवैनं स्पृणाति ।
4.10.e: And for whom one knowing thus enters upon the nidhana, him he rescues from that fetter of death which is in his marrow, s. = IV. 9. 9.
4.10.m: Then, for whom one knowing thus reaches the nidhana, whatever noose of death is in his marrow, he rescues him from that.

4.10.s: evaṃ vā evaṃvid udgātā yajamānasya prāṇebhyo 'dhi mṛtyupāśān unmucyāthainaṃ sāṅgaṃ satanuṃ sarvamṛtyos spṛṇāti |
4.10.d: एवं वा एवंविद् उद्गाता यजमानस्य प्राणेभ्यो ऽधि मृत्युपाशान् उन्मुच्याथैनं साङ्गं सतनुं सर्वमृत्योस् स्पृणाति ।
4.10.m: Thus indeed the udgātṛ who knows thus, having released the nooses of death from the sacrificer's vital breaths, then rescues him, with all his limbs and with his body, from all death.

4.10.s: tad āhus sa vā udgātā yo yajamānasya prāṇebhyo 'dhi mṛtyupāśān unmucyāthainaṃ sāṅgaṃ satanuṃ sarvamṛtyos spṛtvā svarge loke saptadhā dadhātīti |
4.10.d: तद् आहुस् स वा उद्गाता यो यजमानस्य प्राणेभ्यो ऽधि मृत्युपाशान् उन्मुच्याथैनं साङ्गं सतनुं सर्वमृत्योस् स्पृत्वा स्वर्गे लोके सप्तधा दधातीति ।
4.10.e: This they say: "Verily he is the udgdtar who, having released the fetters of death from the breaths of the sacrificer, having then rescued him with his limbs, with his body, from every death, placeth him in seven parts in the heavenly world."
4.10.m: Regarding this they say: 'He indeed is an udgātṛ who, having released the nooses of death from the sacrificer's vital breaths and then having rescued him, with all his limbs and with his body, from all death, places him sevenfold in the heavenly world.'

4.10.s: sa vā eṣa indro vaimṛdha udyan bhavati savitodito mitras saṃgavakāla indro vaikuṇṭho madhyandine samāvartamānaś śarva ugro devo lohitāyan prajāpatir eva saṃveśe 'stamitaḥ |
4.10.d: स वा एष इन्द्रो वैमृध उद्यन् भवति सवितोदितो मित्रस् संगवकाल इन्द्रो वैकुण्ठो मध्यन्दिने समावर्तमानश् शर्व उग्रो देवो लोहितायन् प्रजापतिर् एव संवेशे ऽस्तमितः ।
4.10.e: That same one, rising, is Indra Vaimrdha; risen, Savitar; Mitra at the time when the cows are driven together; Indra Vaikuntha at noon; when returning, ^^Śva; when it is becoming red, the formidable god; Prajapati when it has gone home to lie down.
4.10.m: He indeed, rising, is Indra the repeller of foes; risen, he is Savitṛ; at mid-morning cattle-gathering time, he is Mitra; at midday, turning around, he is Indra Vaikuṇṭha; turning red, he is Śarva the fierce god; at resting, set, he is Prajāpati himself.

4.10.s: tad yasyaivaṃ vidvān hiṅkaroti ya evāsyodyatas svargo lokas tasminn evainaṃ dadhāti |
4.10.d: तद् यस्यैवं विद्वान् हिङ्करोति य एवास्योद्यतस् स्वर्गो लोकस् तस्मिन्न् एवैनं दधाति ।
4.10.e: Thus for whom one knowing thus utters the hinkdra, what heavenly world there is of him rising, in that he thus places him.
4.10.m: Therefore, for whom one knowing thus makes the hiṅkāra, whatever heavenly world is his as [the sun] is rising, in that he places him.

4.10.s: atha yasyaivaṃ vidvān prastauti ya evāsyodite svargo lokas tasminn evainaṃ dadhāti |
4.10.d: अथ यस्यैवं विद्वान् प्रस्तौति य एवास्योदिते स्वर्गो लोकस् तस्मिन्न् एवैनं दधाति ।
4.10.e: And for whom one knowing thus sings the prastāva, what heavenly world there is of him when he has risen, in that he thus places him.
4.10.m: Then, for whom one knowing thus chants the prastāva, whatever heavenly world is his as [the sun] has risen, in that he places him.

4.10.s: atha yasyaivaṃ vidvān ādim ādatte ya evāsya saṃgavakāle svargo lokas tasminn evainaṃ dadhāti |
4.10.d: अथ यस्यैवं विद्वान् आदिम् आदत्ते य एवास्य संगवकाले स्वर्गो लोकस् तस्मिन्न् एवैनं दधाति ।
4.10.e: And for whom one know10. ' &«-. 'Śya. Śsambhavak-. ■*-« prim, m., corrected to-o. '-a. ing thus begins the ddi, what heavenly world there is of him at the time when the cows are driven together, in that he thus places him.
4.10.m: Then, for whom one knowing thus takes up the ādi, whatever heavenly world is his at cattle-gathering time, in that he places him.

4.10.s: atha yasyaivaṃ vidvān udgāyati ya evāsya madhyandine svargo lokas tasminn evainaṃ dadhāti |
4.10.d: अथ यस्यैवं विद्वान् उद्गायति य एवास्य मध्यन्दिने स्वर्गो लोकस् तस्मिन्न् एवैनं दधाति ।
4.10.e: And for whom one knowing thus sings the udgītha, what heavenly world there is of him at noon, in that he thus places him.
4.10.m: Then, for whom one knowing thus chants the udgītha, whatever heavenly world is his at midday, in that he places him.

4.10.s: atha yasyaivaṃ vidvān pratiharati ya evāsyāparāhṇe svargo lokas tasminn evainaṃ dadhāti |
4.10.d: अथ यस्यैवं विद्वान् प्रतिहरति य एवास्यापराह्णे स्वर्गो लोकस् तस्मिन्न् एवैनं दधाति ।
4.10.e: And for whom one knowing thus sings the pratihāra, what heavenly world there is of him in the afternoon, in that he thus places him.
4.10.m: Then, for whom one knowing thus chants the pratihāra, whatever heavenly world is his in the afternoon, in that he places him.

4.10.s: atha yasyaivaṃ vidvān upadravati ya evāsyāstaṃyatas svargo lokas tasminn evainaṃ dadhāti |
4.10.d: अथ यस्यैवं विद्वान् उपद्रवति य एवास्यास्तंयतस् स्वर्गो लोकस् तस्मिन्न् एवैनं दधाति ।
4.10.e: And for whom one knowing thus sings the upadrava, what heavenly world there is of him going home (setting), in that he thus places him.
4.10.m: Then, for whom one knowing thus chants the upadrava, whatever heavenly world is his as [the sun] is setting, in that he places him.

4.10.s: atha yasyaivaṃ vidvān nidhanam upaiti ya evāsyāstamite svargo lokas tasminn evainaṃ dadhāti |
4.10.d: अथ यस्यैवं विद्वान् निधनम् उपैति य एवास्यास्तमिते स्वर्गो लोकस् तस्मिन्न् एवैनं दधाति ।
4.10.e: And for whom one knowing thus enters upon the nidhana, what heavenly world there is of him when he has set, in that he thus places him.
4.10.m: Then, for whom one knowing thus reaches the nidhana, whatever heavenly world is his as [the sun] has set, in that he places him.

4.10.s: evaṃ vā evaṃvid udgātā yajamānasya prāṇebhyo 'dhi mṛtyupāśān unmucyāthainaṃ sāṅgaṃ satanuṃ sarvamṛtyos spṛtvā svarge loke saptadhā dadhāti | saptame 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ | saptamo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
4.10.d: एवं वा एवंविद् उद्गाता यजमानस्य प्राणेभ्यो ऽधि मृत्युपाशान् उन्मुच्याथैनं साङ्गं सतनुं सर्वमृत्योस् स्पृत्वा स्वर्गे लोके सप्तधा दधाति । सप्तमे ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः । सप्तमो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
4.10.e: Even so an udgdtar knowing thus, having released the fetters of death from the breaths of the sacrificer, having then rescued him with his limbs, with his body, from every death, places him in seven parts in the heavenly world.
4.10.m:
Thus indeed the udgātṛ who knows thus, having released the nooses of death from the sacrificer's vital breaths and then having rescued him, with all his limbs and with his body, from all death, places him sevenfold in the heavenly world.
Second khaṇḍa in the seventh anuvāka.
The seventh anuvāka is completed.

4.11.s: ṣaḍ ḍha vai devatās svayambhuvo 'gnir vāyur asāv ādityaḥ prāṇo 'nnaṃ vāk |
4.11.d: षड् ढ वै देवतास् स्वयम्भुवो ऽग्निर् वायुर् असाव् आदित्यः प्राणो ऽन्नं वाक् ।
4.11.e: Verily there are six self-existing divinities, viz. Agni, Vayu, yonder sun, breath, food, speech,
4.11.m: Six indeed are the self-existent deities: Agni, Vāyu, yonder Āditya, breath, food, and speech.

4.11.s: tāś śraiṣṭhye vyavadantāhaṃ śreṣṭhāsmy ahaṃ śreṣṭhāsmy māṃ śriyam upādhvam iti |
4.11.d: ताश् श्रैष्ठ्ये व्यवदन्ताहं श्रेष्ठास्म्य् अहं श्रेष्ठास्म्य् मां श्रियम् उपाध्वम् इति ।
4.11.e: These disputed regarding their preeminence [saying]: " I am the best, I am the best; worship me as excellence."
4.11.m: They disputed for supremacy: 'I am the best! I am the best! Serve me as [your] glory!'

4.11.s: tā anyonyasyai śreṣṭhatāyai nātiṣṭhanta tā abruvan na vā anyonyasyai śreṣṭhatāyai tiṣṭhāmaha etā samprabravāmahai yathā śreṣṭhās sma iti |
4.11.d: ता अन्योन्यस्यै श्रेष्ठतायै नातिष्ठन्त ता अब्रुवन् न वा अन्योन्यस्यै श्रेष्ठतायै तिष्ठामह एता सम्प्रब्रवामहै यथा श्रेष्ठास् स्म इति ।
4.11.e: They did not recognize each the other's preeminence. They said: "Verily we do not recognize each the other's preeminence. Let us therefore explain together how we are best."
4.11.m:
They did not yield to one another's supremacy.
They said: 'We do not yield to one another's supremacy. Come, let us explain together how we are the best.'

4.11.s: tā agnim abruvan kathaṃ tvaṃ śreṣṭho 'sīti |
4.11.d: ता अग्निम् अब्रुवन् कथं त्वं श्रेष्ठो ऽसीति ।
4.11.e: They said to Agni: "How art 210 //. Oertel,, thou the best?"
4.11.m: They said to Agni: 'How are you the best?'

4.11.s: so 'bravīd ahaṃ devānām mukham asmy aham anyāsām prajānām mayāhutayo hūyante ahaṃ devānām annaṃ vikaromy aham manuṣyāṇām |
4.11.d: सो ऽब्रवीद् अहं देवानाम् मुखम् अस्म्य् अहम् अन्यासाम् प्रजानाम् मयाहुतयो हूयन्ते अहं देवानाम् अन्नं विकरोम्य् अहम् मनुष्याणाम् ।
4.11.e: He said: " I am the mouth of the gods, I of the other creatures; by me offerings are offered; I transform the food of the gods, I [that] of men.

4.11.s: sa yan na syām amukhā eva devās syur amukhā anyāḥ prajāḥ nāhutayo hūyeran na devānām annaṃ vikriyeta na manuṣyāṇām |
4.11.d: स यन् न स्याम् अमुखा एव देवास् स्युर् अमुखा अन्याः प्रजाः नाहुतयो हूयेरन् न देवानाम् अन्नं विक्रियेत न मनुष्याणाम् ।
4.11.e: If I were not, the gods would be mouthless, mouthless the other creatures; no offerings would be offered. Neither the food of the gods would be transformed nor [that] of men.

4.11.s: tata idaṃ sarvam parābhavet tato na kiṃ cana pariśiṣyeteti |
4.11.d: तत इदं सर्वम् पराभवेत् ततो न किं चन परिशिष्येतेति ।
4.11.e: Thence this all would perish; thence nothing at all would be left."
4.11.m: Then all this would perish; then nothing at all would be left over.'

4.11.s: evam eveti hocur naiveha kiṃ cana pariśiṣyeta yat tvaṃ na syā iti |
4.11.d: एवम् एवेति होचुर् नैवेह किं चन परिशिष्येत यत् त्वं न स्या इति ।
4.11.e: "Just so," they said; " nothing at all would be left if thou wert not."
4.11.m:
They said: 'Just so! Nothing at all would be left over here if you were not.'
First khaṇḍa in the eighth anuvāka.

4.11.s: atha vāyum abruvan katham u tvaṃ śreṣṭho 'sīti |
4.11.d: अथ वायुम् अब्रुवन् कथम् उ त्वं श्रेष्ठो ऽसीति ।
4.11.e: Then they said to Vayu: " And how art thou the best?"
4.11.m: Then they said to Vāyu: 'And how are you the best?'

4.11.s: so 'bravīd ahaṃ devānām prāṇo 'smy aham anyāsām prajānām yasmād aham utkrāmāmi tatas sa praplavate |
4.11.d: सो ऽब्रवीद् अहं देवानाम् प्राणो ऽस्म्य् अहम् अन्यासाम् प्रजानाम् यस्माद् अहम् उत्क्रामामि ततस् स प्रप्लवते ।
4.11.e: He said: " I am the breath of the gods, I of the other creatures. From whom 1 go out, he then drifts away." ii. =7. 12. = 8.
4.11.m:
He said: 'I am the breath of the gods; I am [the breath] of other creatures.
From whichever [creature] I depart, that one floats away.

4.11.s: sa yad ahaṃ na syāṃ tata idaṃ sarvam parābhavet tato na kiṃ cana pariśiṣyeteti |
4.11.d: स यद् अहं न स्यां तत इदं सर्वम् पराभवेत् ततो न किं चन परिशिष्येतेति ।
4.11.m: If I were not, then all this would perish; then nothing at all would be left over.'

4.11.s: evam eveti hocur naiveha kiṃ cana pariśiṣyeta yat tvaṃ na syā iti | aṣṭame 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
4.11.d: एवम् एवेति होचुर् नैवेह किं चन परिशिष्येत यत् त्वं न स्या इति । अष्टमे ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
4.11.m: They said: 'Just so! Nothing at all would be left over here if you were not.'

4.12.s: athādityam abruvan katham u tvaṃ śreṣṭho 'sīti |
4.12.d: अथादित्यम् अब्रुवन् कथम् उ त्वं श्रेष्ठो ऽसीति ।
4.12.e: Then they said to the sun: "And how art thou the best?"
4.12.m: Then they said to Āditya: 'And how are you the best?'

4.12.s: so 'bravīd aham evodyann ahar bhavāmy aham astaṃyan rātriḥ mayā cakṣuṣā karmāṇi kriyante sa yad ahaṃ na syāṃ naivāhas syān na rātriḥ na karmāṇi kriyeran |
4.12.d: सो ऽब्रवीद् अहम् एवोद्यन्न् अहर् भवाम्य् अहम् अस्तंयन् रात्रिः मया चक्षुषा कर्माणि क्रियन्ते स यद् अहं न स्यां नैवाहस् स्यान् न रात्रिः न कर्माणि क्रियेरन् ।
4.12.e: He said: " I, rising, become the day; I, setting, the night. By me as sight deeds are done. If I were not, there would be no day, no night; no deeds would be done." s. = 11.7. 4. = 11. 8.
4.12.m:
He said: 'Rising, I myself become the day; setting, [I become] the night.
Through me as sight rituals are performed.
If I were not, there would be neither day nor night;
rituals would not be performed.

4.12.s: tata idaṃ sarvam parābhavet tato na kiṃ cana pariśiṣyeteti |
4.12.d: तत इदं सर्वम् पराभवेत् ततो न किं चन परिशिष्येतेति ।
4.12.m: Then all this would perish; then nothing at all would be left over.'

4.12.s: evam eveti hocur naiveha kiṃ cana pariśiṣyeta yat tvaṃ na syā iti |
4.12.d: एवम् एवेति होचुर् नैवेह किं चन परिशिष्येत यत् त्वं न स्या इति ।
4.12.m: They said: 'Just so! Nothing at all would be left over here if you were not.'

4.12.s: atha prāṇam abruvan katham u tvaṃ śreṣṭho 'sīti |
4.12.d: अथ प्राणम् अब्रुवन् कथम् उ त्वं श्रेष्ठो ऽसीति ।
4.12.e: Then they said to breath: " And how art thou the best?" «, He said: " As breath, Agni shineth; as breath, Vayu permeateth space; as breath, the sun riseth; from breath [cometh] food, from breath speech.
4.12.m: Then they said to breath: 'And how are you the best?'

4.12.s: so 'bravīt prāṇo bhūtvāgnir dīpyate prāṇo bhūtvā vāyur ākāśam anubhavati prāṇo bhūtvāditya udeti prāṇād annam prāṇād vāk |
4.12.d: सो ऽब्रवीत् प्राणो भूत्वाग्निर् दीप्यते प्राणो भूत्वा वायुर् आकाशम् अनुभवति प्राणो भूत्वादित्य उदेति प्राणाद् अन्नम् प्राणाद् वाक् ।

4.12.s: sa yad ahaṃ na syāṃ tata idaṃ sarvam parābhavet tato na kiṃ cana pariśiṣyeteti |
4.12.d: स यद् अहं न स्यां तत इदं सर्वम् पराभवेत् ततो न किं चन परिशिष्येतेति ।
4.12.e: If I were not, then this all would perish, then nothing at all would be left." 8. = 11. a.
4.12.m: If I were not, then all this would perish; then nothing at all would be left over.'

4.12.s: evam eveti hocur naiveha kiṃ cana pariśiṣyeta yat tvaṃ na syā iti |
4.12.d: एवम् एवेति होचुर् नैवेह किं चन परिशिष्येत यत् त्वं न स्या इति ।
4.12.m: They said: 'Just so! Nothing at all would be left over here if you were not.'

4.12.s: athānnam abruvan katham u tvaṃ śreṣṭham asīti |
4.12.d: अथान्नम् अब्रुवन् कथम् उ त्वं श्रेष्ठम् असीति ।
4.12.e: Then they said to food: " And how art thou the best?"
4.12.m: Then they said to food: 'And how are you the best?'

4.12.s: tad abravīn mayi pratiṣṭhāyāgnir dīpyate mayi pratiṣṭhāya vāyur ākāśam anuvibhavati mayi pratiṣṭhāyāditya udeti mad eva prāṇo mad vāk |
4.12.d: तद् अब्रवीन् मयि प्रतिष्ठायाग्निर् दीप्यते मयि प्रतिष्ठाय वायुर् आकाशम् अनुविभवति मयि प्रतिष्ठायादित्य उदेति मद् एव प्राणो मद् वाक् ।
4.12.e: It said: "In me standing firm, Agni shineth; in me standing firm, Vayu permeateth space in various directions; in me standing firm, the sun riseth; from me [cometh] breath, from me food." 11. = ] 1. 7. 12. = II. 8.

4.12.s: sa yad ahaṃ na syāṃ tata idaṃ sarvam parābhavet tato na kiṃ cana pariśiṣyeteti |
4.12.d: स यद् अहं न स्यां तत इदं सर्वम् पराभवेत् ततो न किं चन परिशिष्येतेति ।
4.12.m: "If I were not here, this whole world would perish, and nothing at all would remain behind."

4.12.s: evam eveti hocur naiveva kiṃ cana pariśiṣyeta yat tvaṃ na syā iti |
4.12.d: एवम् एवेति होचुर् नैवेव किं चन परिशिष्येत यत् त्वं न स्या इति ।
4.12.m: "Just so," they said, "nothing at all would remain behind if you were not here."

4.12.s: atha vācam abruvan katham u tvaṃ śreṣṭhāsīti |
4.12.d: अथ वाचम् अब्रुवन् कथम् उ त्वं श्रेष्ठासीति ।
4.12.e: They said to speech: " And how art thou the best?"
4.12.m: Then they said to speech: "And how are you the best?"

4.12.s: sābravīn mayaivedaṃ vijñāyate mayādaḥ sa yad ahaṃ na syāṃ naivedaṃ vijñāyeta nādaḥ |
4.12.d: साब्रवीन् मयैवेदं विज्ञायते मयादः स यद् अहं न स्यां नैवेदं विज्ञायेत नादः ।
4.12.e: It said: " By me this is distinguished, by me that. If I were not, neither would this be distinguished nor that." 18. = 11. 7. 16. =: 11. 8.
4.12.m: She said: "By me alone is this discerned, by me that. If I were not here, neither this would be discerned nor that.

4.12.s: tata idaṃ sarvam parābhaven naiveha kiṃ cana pariśiṣyeteti |
4.12.d: तत इदं सर्वम् पराभवेन् नैवेह किं चन परिशिष्येतेति ।
4.12.m: Then this whole world would perish; nothing at all would remain behind here."

4.12.s: evam eveti hocur naiveha kiṃ cana pariśiṣyeta yat tvaṃ na syā iti | aṣṭame 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
4.12.d: एवम् एवेति होचुर् नैवेह किं चन परिशिष्येत यत् त्वं न स्या इति । अष्टमे ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः ।
4.12.m: "Just so," they said, "nothing at all would remain behind here if you were not here." / Second khaṇḍa in the eighth anuvāka.

4.13.s: tā abruvann etā vai kila sarvā devatāḥ ekaikām evānu smaḥ sa yan nu nas sarvāsāṃ devatānām ekā cana na syāt tata idaṃ sarvam parābhavet tato na kiṃ cana pariśiṣyeta hanta sārdhaṃ sametya yac chreṣṭhaṃ tad asāmeti |
4.13.d: ता अब्रुवन्न् एता वै किल सर्वा देवताः एकैकाम् एवानु स्मः स यन् नु नस् सर्वासां देवतानाम् एका चन न स्यात् तत इदं सर्वम् पराभवेत् ततो न किं चन परिशिष्येत हन्त सार्धं समेत्य यच् छ्रेष्ठं तद् असामेति ।
4.13.e: They said: " Verily these are complete divinities. We are dependent each upon each. Now if of us complete divinities any one were not, then this all would perish, then nothing at all would be left. Come, coming together let us be that which is best."
4.13.m: They said: "All these deities indeed—we are one after another. If not even one of us, of all these deities, were here, this whole world would perish, and nothing at all would remain behind. Come, let us unite together and become that which is the best."

4.13.s: tā etasmin prāṇa okāre vācy akāre samāyan tad yat samāyan tat sāmnas sāmatvam |
4.13.d: ता एतस्मिन् प्राण ओकारे वाच्य् अकारे समायन् तद् यत् समायन् तत् साम्नस् सामत्वम् ।
4.13.e: They came together in this breath, in the sound o, [and] in speech, in the sound a. Because they came together (y'i + satn), therefore the sāman is called so."
4.13.m: They came together in this breath as the syllable o, [and] in speech as the syllable a. That they came together (sam-āyan), that is the sāman-nature of the sāman.

4.13.s: tā abruvan yāni no martyāny anapahatapāpmāny akṣarāṇi tāny uddhṛtyāmṛteṣv apahatapāpmasu śuddheṣv akṣareṣu gāyatraṃ gāyāmāgnau vāyāv āditye prāṇe 'nne vāci tenāpahatya mṛtyum apahatya pāpmānaṃ svargaṃ lokam iyāmeti |
4.13.d: ता अब्रुवन् यानि नो मर्त्यान्य् अनपहतपाप्मान्य् अक्षराणि तान्य् उद्धृत्यामृतेष्व् अपहतपाप्मसु शुद्धेष्व् अक्षरेषु गायत्रं गायामाग्नौ वायाव् आदित्ये प्राणे ऽन्ने वाचि तेनापहत्य मृत्युम् अपहत्य पाप्मानं स्वर्गं लोकम् इयामेति ।
4.13.e: They said: " Removing those syllables of us which are mortal, whose evil is not smitten away, let us sing a gāyatra in the syllables [which are] immortal, having evil smitten away, pure: in Agni, in Vayu, in the sun, in breath, in food, in speech. Thereby having smitten away death, having smitten away evil, may we go to the heavenly world."
4.13.m: They said: "Taking out those of our syllables that are mortal and not free from evil, let us sing the gāyatra chant upon the immortal, evil-free, pure syllables—in Agni, in Vāyu, in Āditya, in breath, in food, [and] in speech. Having thereby struck away death, having struck away evil, let us go to the heavenly world."

4.13.s: ety agner amṛtam apahatapāpma śuddham akṣaram gnir ity asya martyam anapahatapāpmākṣaram |
4.13.d: एत्य् अग्नेर् अमृतम् अपहतपाप्म शुद्धम् अक्षरम् ग्निर् इत्य् अस्य मर्त्यम् अनपहतपाप्माक्षरम् ।
4.13.e: A is the syllable of Agni [which is] immortal, having evil smitten away, pure; gnis is his syllable [which is] mortal, not having evil smitten away.
4.13.m: "A" is the immortal, evil-free, pure syllable of Agni; "gniḥ" is his mortal, evil-bound syllable.

4.13.s: veti vāyor amṛtam apahatapāpma śuddham akṣaram yur ity asya martyam anapahatapāpmākṣaram |
4.13.d: वेति वायोर् अमृतम् अपहतपाप्म शुद्धम् अक्षरम् युर् इत्य् अस्य मर्त्यम् अनपहतपाप्माक्षरम् ।
4.13.e: Yd is the syllable of Vayu [which is] immortal, having evil smitten away, pure; yus is his syllable [which is] mortal, not having evil smitten away.
4.13.m: "Vā" is the immortal, evil-free, pure syllable of Vāyu; "yuḥ" is his mortal, evil-bound syllable.

4.13.s: ety ādityasyāmṛtam apahatapāpma śuddham akṣaram tyety asya martyam anapahatapāpmākṣaram |
4.13.d: एत्य् आदित्यस्यामृतम् अपहतपाप्म शुद्धम् अक्षरम् त्येत्य् अस्य मर्त्यम् अनपहतपाप्माक्षरम् ।
4.13.e: A is the syllable of the sun [which is] immortal, having evil smitten away, pure; tya is his syllable [which is] mortal, not having evil smitten away.
4.13.m: "Ā" is the immortal, evil-free, pure syllable of Āditya; "dityaḥ" is his mortal, evil-bound syllable.

4.13.s: preti prāṇasyāmṛtam apahatapāpma śuddham akṣaram ṇety asya martyam anapahatapāpmākṣaram |
4.13.d: प्रेति प्राणस्यामृतम् अपहतपाप्म शुद्धम् अक्षरम् णेत्य् अस्य मर्त्यम् अनपहतपाप्माक्षरम् ।
4.13.e: Prd is the syllable of breath [which is] immortal, having evil smitten away, pure; na is his syllable [which is] mortal, not having evil smitten away.
4.13.m: "Prā" is the immortal, evil-free, pure syllable of breath; "ṇaḥ" is its mortal, evil-bound syllable.

4.13.s: ety annasyāmṛtam apahatapāpma śuddham akṣaram nam ity asya martyam anapahatapāpmākṣaram |
4.13.d: एत्य् अन्नस्यामृतम् अपहतपाप्म शुद्धम् अक्षरम् नम् इत्य् अस्य मर्त्यम् अनपहतपाप्माक्षरम् ।
4.13.e: A is the syllable of food [which is] immortal, having evil smitten away, pure; nam is its syllable [which isj mortal, not having evil smitten away.
4.13.m: "A" is the immortal, evil-free, pure syllable of food; "nnam" is its mortal, evil-bound syllable.

4.13.s: veti vāco 'mṛtam apahatapāpma śuddham akṣaram g ity asyai martyam anapahatapāpmākṣaram |
4.13.d: वेति वाचो ऽमृतम् अपहतपाप्म शुद्धम् अक्षरम् ग् इत्य् अस्यै मर्त्यम् अनपहतपाप्माक्षरम् ।
4.13.e: Vd is the syllable of speech [which is] immortal, having evil smitten away, pure; c is its syllable [which is] mortal, not having evil smitten away.
4.13.m: "Vā" is the immortal, evil-free, pure syllable of speech; "k" is her mortal, evil-bound syllable.

4.13.s: tā etāni martyāny anapahatapāpmāny akṣarāṇy uddhṛtyāmṛteṣv apahatapāpmasu śuddheṣv akṣareṣu gāyatram āgāyann agnau vāyāv āditye prāṇe 'nne vāci tenāpahatya mṛtyum apahatya pāpmānaṃ svargaṃ lokam āyan |
4.13.d: ता एतानि मर्त्यान्य् अनपहतपाप्मान्य् अक्षराण्य् उद्धृत्यामृतेष्व् अपहतपाप्मसु शुद्धेष्व् अक्षरेषु गायत्रम् आगायन्न् अग्नौ वायाव् आदित्ये प्राणे ऽन्ने वाचि तेनापहत्य मृत्युम् अपहत्य पाप्मानं स्वर्गं लोकम् आयन् ।
4.13.e: They, removing those syllables [which are] mortal, not having evil smitten away, sang the gāyatra in the syllables [which are] immortal, having evil smitten away, pure: in Agni, in Vayu, in the sun, in breath, in food, in speech. Thereby having smitten away death, having smitten away evil, they went to the heavenly world,
4.13.m: Taking out these mortal syllables not free from evil, they sang the gāyatra chant upon the immortal, evil-free, pure syllables—in Agni, in Vāyu, in Āditya, in breath, in food, [and] in speech. Having thereby struck away death, having struck away evil, they went to the heavenly world.

4.13.s: apahatya mṛtyum apahatya pāpmānaṃ svargaṃ lokam eti ya evaṃ veda | aṣṭame 'nuvāke tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
4.13.d: अपहत्य मृत्युम् अपहत्य पाप्मानं स्वर्गं लोकम् एति य एवं वेद । अष्टमे ऽनुवाके तृतीयः खण्डः ।
4.13.e: Having smitten away death, having smitten away evil, he goes to the heavenly world who knows thus.
4.13.m: Having struck away death, having struck away evil, he goes to the heavenly world who knows thus. / Third khaṇḍa in the eighth anuvāka.

4.14.s: tā brahmābruvan tvayi pratiṣṭhāyaitam udyacchāmeti tā brahmābravīd āsyena prāṇena yuṣmān āsyena prāṇena mām upāpnavātheti |
4.14.d: ता ब्रह्माब्रुवन् त्वयि प्रतिष्ठायैतम् उद्यच्छामेति ता ब्रह्माब्रवीद् आस्येन प्राणेन युष्मान् आस्येन प्राणेन माम् उपाप्नवाथेति ।
4.14.e: They said to the brahman: "Standing firm in thee we will hold this one up." To them the brahman said: " With the breath in the mouth ye shall obtain yourselves, with the breath in the mouth me."
4.14.m: They said to brahman: "Resting upon you, let us raise this [chant]." Brahman said to them: "Through the breath of the mouth you shall reach each other, through the breath of the mouth you shall reach me."

4.14.s: tā etena prāṇenaukāreṇa vācy akāram abhinimeṣyantyo hiṅkārād bhakāram okāreṇa vācam anusvarantya ubhābhyām prāṇābhyāṃ gāyatram agāyann ovā3c ovā3c ovā3c hum bhā vo vā iti |
4.14.d: ता एतेन प्राणेनौकारेण वाच्य् अकारम् अभिनिमेष्यन्त्यो हिङ्काराद् भकारम् ओकारेण वाचम् अनुस्वरन्त्य उभाभ्याम् प्राणाभ्यां गायत्रम् अगायन्न् ओवा3च् ओवा3च् ओवा3च् हुम् भा वो वा इति ।
4.14.e: They, by this breath, the o-sound, being about to settle the a-sound in speech, and by the o-sound sounding the Ma-sound as speech after the hinkdra, sang the gāyatra with both these breaths: ovdSc ovdSc ovdSc hum bhd vo vd.
4.14.m: With this breath as the syllable o, closing in upon the syllable a in speech, sounding speech from the hiṅkāra to the sound bha with the syllable o, they sang the gāyatra chant with both breaths: "ovā3c ovā3c ovā3c hum bhā vo vā".

4.14.s: sa yathobhayāpadī pratitiṣṭhaty evam eva svarge loke pratyatiṣṭhan prati svarge loke tiṣṭhati ya evaṃ veda |
4.14.d: स यथोभयापदी प्रतितिष्ठत्य् एवम् एव स्वर्गे लोके प्रत्यतिष्ठन् प्रति स्वर्गे लोके तिष्ठति य एवं वेद ।
4.14.e: As one with both feet stands firm, even so they stood firm in the heavenly world. He stands firm in the heavenly world who knows thus.
4.14.m: Just as a two-footed creature stands firm, even so they stood firm in the heavenly world. He stands firm in the heavenly world who knows thus.

4.14.s: ya u ha vā evaṃvid asmāl lokāt praiti sa prāṇa eva bhūtvā vāyum apyeti vāyor adhy abhrāṇy abhrebhyo 'dhi vṛṣṭiṃ vṛṣṭyaivemaṃ lokam anuvibhavati |
4.14.d: य उ ह वा एवंविद् अस्माल् लोकात् प्रैति स प्राण एव भूत्वा वायुम् अप्येति वायोर् अध्य् अभ्राण्य् अभ्रेभ्यो ऽधि वृष्टिं वृष्ट्यैवेमं लोकम् अनुविभवति ।
4.14.e: And he who knowing thus departs from this world, he, having become breath, goes unto Vayu, from Vayu unto the clouds, from the clouds unto rain. With rain he extends over this world,
4.14.m: And whoever, knowing thus, departs from this world, becoming breath alone, he enters Vāyu; from Vāyu into the clouds; from the clouds into rain; through the rain alone he pervades this world.

4.14.s: ṛṣayo ha sattram āsāṃ cakrire te punaḥ-punar bahvībhir-bahvībhiḥ pratipadbhis svargasya lokasya dvāraṃ nānu cana bubudhire |
4.14.d: ऋषयो ह सत्त्रम् आसां चक्रिरे ते पुनः-पुनर् बह्वीभिर्-बह्वीभिः प्रतिपद्भिस् स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य द्वारं नानु चन बुबुधिरे ।
4.14.e: The sages (rsi) sat a session (sattra). They again and again with many, many introductory stanzas did in no way perceive the door of the heavenly world,
4.14.m: The sages performed a sacrificial session. Time and again, through very many introductory verses, they did not perceive the door to the heavenly world.

4.14.s: ta u śrameṇa tapasā vratacaryeṇendram avarurudhire |
4.14.d: त उ श्रमेण तपसा व्रतचर्येणेन्द्रम् अवरुरुधिरे ।
4.14.e: And they with exertion, with penance, with the performance of vows, got possession of Indra.
4.14.m: Through weariness, ascetic heat, and the observance of vows, they won over Indra.

4.14.s: taṃ hocus svargaṃ vai lokam aipsiṣma te punaḥ-punar bahvībhir-bahvībhiḥ pratipadbhis svargasya lokasya dvāraṃ nānu canābhutsmahi tathā no 'nuśādhi yathā svargasya lokasya dvāram anuprajñāyānārtās svasti saṃvatsarasyodṛcaṃ gatvā svargaṃ lokam iyāmeti |
4.14.d: तं होचुस् स्वर्गं वै लोकम् ऐप्सिष्म ते पुनः-पुनर् बह्वीभिर्-बह्वीभिः प्रतिपद्भिस् स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य द्वारं नानु चनाभुत्स्महि तथा नो ऽनुशाधि यथा स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य द्वारम् अनुप्रज्ञायानार्तास् स्वस्ति संवत्सरस्योदृचं गत्वा स्वर्गं लोकम् इयामेति ।
4.14.e: They said to him: " We have desired to obtain the heavenly world; yet again and again with many, many introductory stanzas have we in no way perceived the door of the heavenly world. Teach us so that we, perceiving the door of the heavenly world, unharmed, having gone successfully to the end of the year, may go to the heavenly world."
4.14.m: They said to him: "We have desired the heavenly world. Time and again, through very many introductory verses, we have not perceived the door to the heavenly world. Instruct us so that, having recognized the door to the heavenly world, unharmed, safely reaching the end of the year, we may go to the heavenly world."

4.14.s: tān hovāca ko vas sthaviratama iti | aṣṭame 'nuvāke caturthaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
4.14.d: तान् होवाच को वस् स्थविरतम इति । अष्टमे ऽनुवाके चतुर्थः खण्डः ।
4.14.e: He said to them: " Who of you is the oldest?"
4.14.m: He said to them: "Who among you is the oldest?" / Fourth khaṇḍa in the eighth anuvāka.

4.15.s: sa vā ehīti hovāca tasmai vai te 'haṃ tad vakṣyāmi yad vidvāṃsas svargasya lokasya dvāram anuprajñāyānārtās svasti saṃvatsarasyodṛcaṃ gatvā svargaṃ lokam eṣyatheti |
4.15.d: स वा एहीति होवाच तस्मै वै ते ऽहं तद् वक्ष्यामि यद् विद्वांसस् स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य द्वारम् अनुप्रज्ञायानार्तास् स्वस्ति संवत्सरस्योदृचं गत्वा स्वर्गं लोकम् एष्यथेति ।
4.15.e: "Then come," he said; "I will tell thee that which knowing ye, perceiving the door of the heavenly world, unharmed, having gone successfully to the end of the year, shall go to the heavenly world."
4.15.m: "Come then," he said; "to you, indeed, I shall speak that by which, knowing it, having recognized the door to the heavenly world, unharmed, safely reaching the end of the year, you will go to the heavenly world."

4.15.s: tasmā etaṃ gāyatrasyodgītham upaniṣadam amṛtam uvācāgnau vāyāv āditye prāṇe 'nne vāci |
4.15.d: तस्मा एतं गायत्रस्योद्गीथम् उपनिषदम् अमृतम् उवाचाग्नौ वायाव् आदित्ये प्राणे ऽन्ने वाचि ।
4.15.e: To him he told this udgītha of the gāyatra[-sdm,an, the upaniṣad, the immortal, in Agni, in Vayu, in the sun, in breath, in food, in speech.
4.15.m: To him he declared this immortal upaniṣad, the udgītha of the gāyatra chant, in Agni, in Vāyu, in Āditya, in breath, in food, [and] in speech.

4.15.s: tato vai te svargasya lokasya dvāram anuprajñāyānārtās svasti saṃvatsarasyodṛcaṃ gatvā svargaṃ lokam āyan |
4.15.d: ततो वै ते स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य द्वारम् अनुप्रज्ञायानार्तास् स्वस्ति संवत्सरस्योदृचं गत्वा स्वर्गं लोकम् आयन् ।
4.15.e: Verily they then, perceiving the door of the heavenly world, unharmed, having gone successfully to the end of the year, went to the heavenly woi-ld.
4.15.m: Then indeed, having recognized the door to the heavenly world, unharmed, safely reaching the end of the year, they went to the heavenly world.

4.15.s: evam evaivaṃ vidvān svargasya lokasya dvāram anuprajñāyānārtas svasti saṃvatsarasyodṛcaṃ gatvā svargaṃ lokam eti | aṣṭame 'nuvāke pañcamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ | aṣṭamo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
4.15.d: एवम् एवैवं विद्वान् स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य द्वारम् अनुप्रज्ञायानार्तस् स्वस्ति संवत्सरस्योदृचं गत्वा स्वर्गं लोकम् एति । अष्टमे ऽनुवाके पञ्चमः खण्डः । अष्टमो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
4.15.e: Even so one knowing thus, perceiving the gate of the heavenly world, unharmed, having gone successfully to the end of the year, goes to the heavenly world.
4.15.m: Even so, one who knows thus, having recognized the door to the heavenly world, unharmed, safely reaching the end of the year, goes to the heavenly world. / Fifth khaṇḍa in the eighth anuvāka. / The eighth anuvāka is completed.

4.16.s: evaṃ vā etaṃ gāyatrasyodgītham upaniṣadam amṛtam indro 'gastyāyovācāgastya iṣāya śyāvāśvaya iṣaś śyāvāśvir gauṣūktaye gauṣūktir jvālāyanāya jvālāyanaś śāṭyāyanaye śāṭyāyanī rāmāya krātujāteyāya vaiyāghrapadyāya rāmaḥ krātujāteyo vaiyāghrapadyaḥ | navame 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
4.16.d: एवं वा एतं गायत्रस्योद्गीथम् उपनिषदम् अमृतम् इन्द्रो ऽगस्त्यायोवाचागस्त्य इषाय श्यावाश्वय इषश् श्यावाश्विर् गौषूक्तये गौषूक्तिर् ज्वालायनाय ज्वालायनश् शाट्यायनये शाट्यायनी रामाय क्रातुजातेयाय वैयाघ्रपद्याय रामः क्रातुजातेयो वैयाघ्रपद्यः । नवमे ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
4.16.e: Verily thus Indra told this ijdg'itha of the gāyatra \-sāman'\, the upaniṣad, the immortal, to Agastya, Agastya to Isa 9ysiva9vi, Isa ()y«\&(}\'i to Gfiusukti, Gausukti to Jvalayana, Jvalayana to Śatyayani, 9Styayani to Rama Kratujateya Vaiyaghrapadya, Rama Kratujateya Vaij'aghrapadya—
4.16.m: Thus, indeed, Indra declared this immortal upaniṣad, the udgītha of the gāyatra chant, to Agastya; Agastya to Iṣa Śyāvāśvaya; Iṣa Śyāvāśvi to Gauṣūkti; Gauṣūkti to Jvālāyana; Jvālāyana to Śāṭyāyani; Śāṭyāyani to Rāma Krātujāteya Vaiyāghrapadya; Rāma Krātujāteya Vaiyāghrapadya— / First khaṇḍa in the ninth anuvāka.

4.17.s: śaṅkhāya bābhravyāya śaṅkho bābhravyo dakṣāya kātyāyanaya ātreyāya dakṣaḥ kātyāyanir ātreyaḥ kaṃsāya vārakyāya kaṃso vārakyas suyajñāya śāṇḍilyāya suyajñaś śāṇḍilyo 'gnidattāya śāṇḍilyāyāgnidattaś śāṇḍilyas suyajñāya śāṇḍilyāya suyajñaś śāṇḍilyo jayantāya vārakyāya jayanto vārakyo janaśrutāya vārakyāya janaśruto vārakyas sudattāya pārāśaryāya |
4.17.d: शङ्खाय बाभ्रव्याय शङ्खो बाभ्रव्यो दक्षाय कात्यायनय आत्रेयाय दक्षः कात्यायनिर् आत्रेयः कंसाय वारक्याय कंसो वारक्यस् सुयज्ञाय शाण्डिल्याय सुयज्ञश् शाण्डिल्यो ऽग्निदत्ताय शाण्डिल्यायाग्निदत्तश् शाण्डिल्यस् सुयज्ञाय शाण्डिल्याय सुयज्ञश् शाण्डिल्यो जयन्ताय वारक्याय जयन्तो वारक्यो जनश्रुताय वारक्याय जनश्रुतो वारक्यस् सुदत्ताय पाराशर्याय ।
4.17.e: — to _9ankha Bfibhravya, Śafikha Babhravya to Daksa Katyfiyaiii Atreya, Daksa Katyfiyani Atreya to Kansa Vfirakji^a, Kansa Vfivakya to Suyajfia Śandilya, Suyajfia (Śfindilya to Jayanta Varakya, Jayanta Vfirakya to Janagnita Varakya, Jana9ruta Varakya to Sudatta ParJi9arya. That same upaniṣad of the gāyatra [sdmanl of Śiity'Śyani is to be worshiped thus.
4.17.m: —to Śaṅkha Bābhravya; Śaṅkha Bābhravya to Dakṣa Kātyāyani Ātreya; Dakṣa Kātyāyani Ātreya to Kaṃsa Vārakya; Kaṃsa Vārakya to Suyajña Śāṇḍilya; Suyajña Śāṇḍilya to Agnidatta Śāṇḍilya; Agnidatta Śāṇḍilya to Suyajña Śāṇḍilya; Suyajña Śāṇḍilya to Jayanta Vārakya; Jayanta Vārakya to Janaśruta Vārakya; Janaśruta Vārakya to Sudatta Pārāśarya.

4.17.s: saiṣā śāṭyāyanī gāyatrasyopaniṣad evam upāsitavyā | navame 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ | navamo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
4.17.d: सैषा शाट्यायनी गायत्रस्योपनिषद् एवम् उपासितव्या । नवमे ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः । नवमो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
4.17.m: This is that Śāṭyāyanī upaniṣad of the gāyatra chant; it is to be meditated upon thus. / Second khaṇḍa in the ninth anuvāka. / The ninth anuvāka is completed.

4.18.s: keneṣitam patati preṣitam manaḥ kena prāṇaḥ prathamaḥ praiti yuktaḥ keneṣitāṃ vācam imāṃ vadanti cakṣuś śrotraṃ ka u devo yunakti |
4.18.d: केनेषितम् पतति प्रेषितम् मनः केन प्राणः प्रथमः प्रैति युक्तः केनेषितां वाचम् इमां वदन्ति चक्षुश् श्रोत्रं क उ देवो युनक्ति ।
4.18.e: Sent by whom does the mind, sent forth, fly? Yoked by whom does the first breath come forth? By whom is this speech sent which they speak? And which god yokes sight [and] hearing?
4.18.m:
"By whom impelled does the mind fly forth sent?
By whom yoked does the first breath move forward?
By whom impelled do they speak this speech?
And what god yokes the eye and the ear?"

4.18.s: śrotrasya śrotram manaso mano yad vāco ha vācaṃ sa u prāṇasya prāṇaḥ cakṣuṣaś cakṣur atimucya dhīrāḥ pretyāsmāl lokād amṛtā bhavanti |
4.18.d: श्रोत्रस्य श्रोत्रम् मनसो मनो यद् वाचो ह वाचं स उ प्राणस्य प्राणः चक्षुषश् चक्षुर् अतिमुच्य धीराः प्रेत्यास्माल् लोकाद् अमृता भवन्ति ।
4.18.e: Released from the hearing of the hearing, from the mind of the mind, from the speech of speech—and that is also the breath of the breath—from the sight of the sight, the wise departing from this world become immortal.
4.18.m:
That which is the ear of the ear, the mind of the mind, the speech of speech, that indeed is the breath of breath,
the eye of the eye. Having relinquished [them], the wise, departing from this world, become immortal.

4.18.s: na tatra cakṣur gacchati na vāg gacchati no manaḥ na vidma na vijānīmo yathaitad anuśiṣyāt |
4.18.d: न तत्र चक्षुर् गच्छति न वाग् गच्छति नो मनः न विद्म न विजानीमो यथैतद् अनुशिष्यात् ।
4.18.e: Sight does not go there, speech does not go there, neither [does] mind. We do not know, we do not distinguish, how one might teach that.
4.18.m:
The eye does not go there, nor does speech go, nor the mind.
We do not know, we do not comprehend how one could instruct this.

4.18.s: anyad eva tad viditād atho aviditād adhi iti śuśruma pūrveṣāṃ ye nas tad vyācacakṣire |
4.18.d: अन्यद् एव तद् विदिताद् अथो अविदिताद् अधि इति शुश्रुम पूर्वेषां ये नस् तद् व्याचचक्षिरे ।
4.18.e: "It is different from the known and likewise from the unknown;" thus we heard from those of old, who explained it to us.
4.18.m:
It is indeed different from the known, and moreover above the unknown.
Thus have we heard from the ancients who explained that to us.

4.18.s: yad vācānabhyuditaṃ yena vāg abhyudyate tad eva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yad idam upāsate |
4.18.d: यद् वाचानभ्युदितं येन वाग् अभ्युद्यते तद् एव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यद् इदम् उपासते ।
4.18.e: That which is not declared by speech, that by which speech is declared, only that know thou as brahman, not that which they worship here.
4.18.m:
That which is not expressed by speech, by which speech is expressed—
know that alone as brahman, not this which they worship here.

4.18.s: yan manasā na manute yenāhur mano matam tad eva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yad idam upāsate |
4.18.d: यन् मनसा न मनुते येनाहुर् मनो मतम् तद् एव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यद् इदम् उपासते ।
4.18.e: That which one does not think with the mind, that by which they say the mind is thought, only that know thou as brahman, not that which they worship here.
4.18.m:
That which one does not think with the mind, by which, they say, the mind is thought—
know that alone as brahman, not this which they worship here.

4.18.s: yac cakṣuṣā na paśyati yena cakṣūṃṣi paśyati tad eva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yad idam upāsate |
4.18.d: यच् चक्षुषा न पश्यति येन चक्षूंषि पश्यति तद् एव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यद् इदम् उपासते ।
4.18.e: That which one does not see with sight, that by which one sees sights, only that know thou as brahman, not that which they worship here.
4.18.m:
That which one does not see with the eye, by which one sees eyes—
know that alone as brahman, not this which they worship here.

4.18.s: yac chrotreṇa na śṛṇoti yena śrotram idaṃ śrutam tad eva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yad idam upāsate |
4.18.d: यच् छ्रोत्रेण न शृणोति येन श्रोत्रम् इदं श्रुतम् तद् एव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यद् इदम् उपासते ।
4.18.e: That which one does not hear with hearing, that by which this hearing is heard, only that know thou as brahman, not that which they worship here.
4.18.m:
That which one does not hear with the ear, by which this ear is heard—
know that alone as brahman, not this which they worship here.

4.18.s: yat prāṇena na prāṇiti yena prāṇaḥ praṇīyate tad eva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yad idam upāsate |
4.18.d: यत् प्राणेन न प्राणिति येन प्राणः प्रणीयते तद् एव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यद् इदम् उपासते ।
4.18.e: That which one does not breathe with breath, that by which breath is led forth, only that know thou as brahman, not that which they worship here.
4.18.m:
That which one does not breathe with breath, by which breath is guided—
know that alone as brahman, not this which they worship here.
The first khaṇḍa in the tenth anuvāka.

4.19.s: yadi manyase su vedeti dahram evāpi nūnaṃ tvaṃ vettha brahmaṇo rūpaṃ yad asya tvaṃ yad asya deveṣu atha nu mīmāṃsyam eva te manye 'viditam |
4.19.d: यदि मन्यसे सु वेदेति दह्रम् एवापि नूनं त्वं वेत्थ ब्रह्मणो रूपं यद् अस्य त्वं यद् अस्य देवेषु अथ नु मीमांस्यम् एव ते मन्ये ऽविदितम् ।
4.19.e: If thou thinkest: " I know [it] well," little dost thou even then know the form of the brahman, what of it thou [art?], what of it [is] among the gods. Now then I think what is unknown is to be pondered upon by thee.
4.19.m:
If you think: "I know [it] well," indeed you surely know only a small form of brahman—what of it is in you, and what of it is among the gods.
Therefore now it is indeed to be investigated by you. I think it is [not yet] understood.

4.19.s: nāham manye su vedeti no na vedeti veda ca yo nas tad veda tad veda no na vedeti veda ca |
4.19.d: नाहम् मन्ये सु वेदेति नो न वेदेति वेद च यो नस् तद् वेद तद् वेद नो न वेदेति वेद च ।
4.19.e: I do not think: "I know [itj well," neither do I know: "I know [it] not." He of us who knows this knows it (the brahman), and he does not know: " I know [it] not."
4.19.m:
I do not think: "I know [it] well," nor: "I do not know." I know it too.
He among us who knows that, knows that; nor does he know: "I do not know," and yet he knows.

4.19.s: yasyāmataṃ tasya matam mataṃ yasya na veda saḥ avijñātaṃ vijānatāṃ avijānatām |
4.19.d: यस्यामतं तस्य मतम् मतं यस्य न वेद सः अविज्ञातं विजानतां अविजानताम् ।
4.19.e: Of whom it is not thought, of him it is thought; of whom it is thought, he knows it not. Not understood [is it] of those who understand; [it is] understood '*,• of those who do not understand;
4.19.m:
He by whom it is unthought, to him it is thought; he to whom it is thought does not know.
It is unknown to those who know; [it is] known to those who do not know.

4.19.s: pratibodhaviditam matam amṛtatvaṃ hi vindate ātmanā vindate vīryaṃ vidyayā vindate 'mṛtam |
4.19.d: प्रतिबोधविदितम् मतम् अमृतत्वं हि विन्दते आत्मना विन्दते वीर्यं विद्यया विन्दते ऽमृतम् ।
4.19.e: It is thought to be known in awakening (?), for one finds immortality; by the self one finds strength, by knowledge one finds immortality,
4.19.m:
When it is known with every awakening, it is comprehended, for [thereby] one finds immortality.
By the self one finds vigor; by knowledge one finds immortality.

4.19.s: iha ced avedīd atha satyam asti na ced ihāvedīn mahatī vinaṣṭiḥ bhūteṣu-bhūteṣu vivicya dhīrāḥ pretyāsmāl lokād amṛtā bhavanti | daśame 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
4.19.d: इह चेद् अवेदीद् अथ सत्यम् अस्ति न चेद् इहावेदीन् महती विनष्टिः भूतेषु-भूतेषु विविच्य धीराः प्रेत्यास्माल् लोकाद् अमृता भवन्ति । दशमे ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः ।
4.19.e: If one has known [it] here, then it is true; and if one has not known [it] here, [there is] great loss. The wise, having separated [it] in the several beings, departing from this world become immortal.
4.19.m:
If one has known it here, then truth exists;
if one has not known it here, great is the destruction.
Distinguishing [it] in each and every being, the wise, departing from this world, become immortal.
The second khaṇḍa in the tenth anuvāka.

4.20.s: brahma ha devebhyo vijigye tasya ha brahmaṇo vijaye devā amahīyanta ta aikṣantāsmākam evāyaṃ vijayaḥ asmākam evāyam mahimeti |
4.20.d: ब्रह्म ह देवेभ्यो विजिग्ये तस्य ह ब्रह्मणो विजये देवा अमहीयन्त त ऐक्षन्तास्माकम् एवायं विजयः अस्माकम् एवायम् महिमेति ।
4.20.e: The brahman won a complete victory for the gods. By the complete victory of this brahman the gods were exalted. They considered: " Ours is this complete victory, ours is this greatness."
4.20.m:
Brahman indeed won a victory for the gods.
In that victory of brahman the gods grew exultant.
They thought: "Ours alone is this victory;
ours alone is this greatness."

4.20.s: tad dhaiṣāṃ vijajñau tebhyo ha prādur babhūva tan na vyajānanta kim idaṃ yakṣam iti |
4.20.d: तद् धैषां विजज्ञौ तेभ्यो ह प्रादुर् बभूव तन् न व्यजानन्त किम् इदं यक्षम् इति ।
4.20.e: Now it (the brahman) became aware of this [thought] of them. It manifested itself to them. They did not recognize it [saying]: " What is this spectre?"
4.20.m:
It knew this [thought] of theirs.
It appeared to them.
They did not know what this wonder was.

4.20.s: te 'gnim abruvañ jātaveda etad vijānīhi kim etad yakṣam iti tatheti |
4.20.d: ते ऽग्निम् अब्रुवञ् जातवेद एतद् विजानीहि किम् एतद् यक्षम् इति तथेति ।
4.20.e: They said to Agni: " O Jfitavedas, find that out, what spectre this is." "Yes."
4.20.m:
They said to Agni: "Jātavedas, find this out: what is this wonder?"
"So be it."

4.20.s: tad abhyadravat tam abhyavadat ko 'sīti agnir vā aham asmīty abravīj jātavedā vā aham asmīti |
4.20.d: तद् अभ्यद्रवत् तम् अभ्यवदत् को ऽसीति अग्निर् वा अहम् अस्मीत्य् अब्रवीज् जातवेदा वा अहम् अस्मीति ।
4.20.e: He ran to it. It said unto him: "Who art thou?" "I am Agni," he said; "I am Jatavedas."
4.20.m:
He ran up to it.
It said to him: "Who are you?"
"I am Agni," he said, "or I am Jātavedas."

4.20.s: tasmiṃs tvayi kiṃ vīryam iti apīdaṃ sarvaṃ daheyam yad idam pṛthivyām iti |
4.20.d: तस्मिंस् त्वयि किं वीर्यम् इति अपीदं सर्वं दहेयम् यद् इदम् पृथिव्याम् इति ।
4.20.e: "What strength then is in thee?" " I could burn even everything which is here on earth."
4.20.m:
"In that you, what is the power?"
"I could burn even all this whatever is here on earth."
