4.20.s: tasmai tṛṇaṃ nidadhāv etad daheti tad upapreyāya sarvajavena tan na śaśāka dagdhum sa tata eva nivavṛte nainad aśakaṃ vijñātuṃ yad etad yakṣam iti |
4.20.d: तस्मै तृणं निदधाव् एतद् दहेति तद् उपप्रेयाय सर्वजवेन तन् न शशाक दग्धुम् स तत एव निववृते नैनद् अशकं विज्ञातुं यद् एतद् यक्षम् इति ।
4.20.e: It put down before him a blade of grass [saying]: "Burn this." Approaching it with all his might he could not burn it. Thereupon he returned [saying]: " I could not find out what spectre this is."
4.20.m:
It placed a blade of grass before him: "Burn this!"
He went up to it with all speed.
He was not able to burn it.
He returned right from there: "I was not able to find out what this wonder is."

4.20.s: atha vāyum abruvan vāyav etad vijānīhi kim etad yakṣam iti tatheti |
4.20.d: अथ वायुम् अब्रुवन् वायव् एतद् विजानीहि किम् एतद् यक्षम् इति तथेति ।
4.20.e: Then they said to Vfiyu: "O Vfiyu, find that out, what spectre this is." " Yes."
4.20.m:
Then they said to Vāyu: "Vāyu, find this out: what is this wonder?"
"So be it."

4.20.s: tad abhyadravat tam abhyavadat ko 'sīti vāyur vā aham asmīty abravīn mātariśvā vā aham asmīti |
4.20.d: तद् अभ्यद्रवत् तम् अभ्यवदत् को ऽसीति वायुर् वा अहम् अस्मीत्य् अब्रवीन् मातरिश्वा वा अहम् अस्मीति ।
4.20.e: He ran to it. " It said unto him: "Who art thou?" "I am Vayu," he said; "I am Matari9van." " What strength then is in thee?" " I could take even everything that is here on earth."
4.20.m:
He ran up to it.
It said to him: "Who are you?"
"I am Vāyu," he said, "or I am Mātariśvan."

4.20.s: tasmiṃs tvayi kiṃ vīryam iti apīdaṃ sarvam ādadīya yad idam pṛthivyām iti |
4.20.d: तस्मिंस् त्वयि किं वीर्यम् इति अपीदं सर्वम् आददीय यद् इदम् पृथिव्याम् इति ।
4.20.e: It put down before him a blade of grass [saying]: "Take this." Approaching it with all his might he could not take it. Thereupon he returned [saying]: "I could not find out what spectre this is."
4.20.m:
"In that you, what is the power?"
"I could seize even all this whatever is here on earth."

4.20.s: tasmai tṛṇaṃ nidadhāv etad ādatsveti tad upapreyāya sarvajavena tan na śaśākādātum sa tata eva nivavṛte nainad aśakaṃ vijñātuṃ yad etad yakṣam iti |
4.20.d: तस्मै तृणं निदधाव् एतद् आदत्स्वेति तद् उपप्रेयाय सर्वजवेन तन् न शशाकादातुम् स तत एव निववृते नैनद् अशकं विज्ञातुं यद् एतद् यक्षम् इति ।
4.20.e: Then they said to Indra: "O Maghavan, find that out, what spectre this is." " Yes." He ran to it. It was concealed from him.
4.20.m:
It placed a blade of grass before him: "Seize this!"
He went up to it with all speed.
He was not able to seize it.
He returned right from there: "I was not able to find out what this wonder is."

4.20.s: athendram abruvan maghavann etad vijānīhi kim etad yakṣam iti tatheti tad abhyadravat tasmāt tiro 'dadhe |
4.20.d: अथेन्द्रम् अब्रुवन् मघवन्न् एतद् विजानीहि किम् एतद् यक्षम् इति तथेति तद् अभ्यद्रवत् तस्मात् तिरो ऽदधे ।
4.20.e: In that same space he encountered a woman, greatly shining, Uma Haimavati. He said to her: "What spectre is this?"
4.20.m:
Then they said to Indra: "Maghavan, find this out: what is this wonder?"
"So be it."
He ran up to it.
It vanished from him.

4.20.s: sa tasminn evākāśe striyam ājagāma bahu śobhamānām umāṃ haimavatīm tāṃ hovāca kim etad yakṣam iti | daśame 'nuvāke tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
4.20.d: स तस्मिन्न् एवाकाशे स्त्रियम् आजगाम बहु शोभमानाम् उमां हैमवतीम् तां होवाच किम् एतद् यक्षम् इति । दशमे ऽनुवाके तृतीयः खण्डः ।
4.20.m:
In that very space he came upon a woman, Umā Haimavatī, shining exceedingly.
He said to her: "What is this wonder?"
The third khaṇḍa in the tenth anuvāka.

4.21.s: brahmeti hovāca brahmaṇo vā etad vijaye mahīyadhva iti tato haiva vidāṃ cakāra brahmeti |
4.21.d: ब्रह्मेति होवाच ब्रह्मणो वा एतद् विजये महीयध्व इति ततो हैव विदां चकार ब्रह्मेति ।
4.21.e: " The JraAmaw," she said; " through the J^-aAwiaw'* complete victory ye are exalted." Then he knew: " [It is] the brahman.'"
4.21.m:
"It is brahman," she said. "In the victory of brahman indeed are you exulting."
Then indeed he came to know: "It is brahman."

4.21.s: tasmād vā ete devā atitarām ivānyān devān yad agnir vāyur indraḥ te hy enan nediṣṭham paspṛśus sa hy enat prathamo vidāṃ cakāra brahmeti |
4.21.d: तस्माद् वा एते देवा अतितराम् इवान्यान् देवान् यद् अग्निर् वायुर् इन्द्रः ते ह्य् एनन् नेदिष्ठम् पस्पृशुस् स ह्य् एनत् प्रथमो विदां चकार ब्रह्मेति ।
4.21.e: Therefore indeed these gods—viz. Agni, Vayu, Indra—are as it were greatly above the other gods. For they touched it nearest; for he first knew it to be the brahman.
4.21.m:
Therefore indeed these gods far surpass, as it were, the other gods—namely, Agni, Vāyu, and Indra;
for they touched it nearest; for he [Indra] first came to know: "It is brahman."

4.21.s: tasmād vā indro 'titarām ivānyān devān sa hy enan nediṣṭham pasparśa sa hy enat prathamo vidāṃ cakāra brahmeti |
4.21.d: तस्माद् वा इन्द्रो ऽतितराम् इवान्यान् देवान् स ह्य् एनन् नेदिष्ठम् पस्पर्श स ह्य् एनत् प्रथमो विदां चकार ब्रह्मेति ।
4.21.e: Therefore indeed Indra is as it were greatly above the other gods. For he touched it nearest; for he first knew it to be the brahman.
4.21.m:
Therefore indeed Indra far surpasses, as it were, the other gods;
for he touched it nearest; for he first came to know: "It is brahman."

4.21.s: tasyaiṣa ādeśo yad etad vidyuto vyadyutad ā3 iti nyamiṣad ā3 ity adhidevatam |
4.21.d: तस्यैष आदेशो यद् एतद् विद्युतो व्यद्युतद् आ3 इति न्यमिषद् आ3 इत्य् अधिदेवतम् ।
4.21.e: Regarding it [there is] this direction: " What of the lightning hath lightened: ah! hath winked: ah!" Thus with regard to the divinities,
4.21.m:
This is its teaching: that which is this flashing of lightning, "Ah!", that it winked, "Ah!"—
thus pertaining to the deities.

4.21.s: athādhyātmam yad enad gacchatīva ca mano 'nena cainad upasmaraty abhīkṣṇaṃ saṃkalpaḥ |
4.21.d: अथाध्यात्मम् यद् एनद् गच्छतीव च मनो ऽनेन चैनद् उपस्मरत्य् अभीक्ष्णं संकल्पः ।
4.21.e: Now with regard to the self. That which both goes as mind, as it were, and through it (mind) imagination continually remembers it (the brahman).
4.21.m:
Now pertaining to the self:
that which the mind goes to, as it were, and by which memory repeatedly recalls it—[that is] intention.

4.21.s: tad dha tadvanaṃ nāma tadvanam ity upāsitavyam sa ya etad evaṃ vedābhi hainaṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāni saṃvāṅchanti |
4.21.d: तद् ध तद्वनं नाम तद्वनम् इत्य् उपासितव्यम् स य एतद् एवं वेदाभि हैनं सर्वाणि भूतानि संवाङ्छन्ति ।
4.21.e: Verily it is tadvana by name. As tadvana it is to be worshiped. Who knows this thus, unto him all beings desire together.
4.21.m:
That is called Tadvana, "the longing for that."
It is to be worshiped as Tadvana.
He who knows this thus, towards him indeed all beings yearn.

4.21.s: upaniṣadam bho brūhīti uktā ta upaniṣat brāhmīṃ vāva ta upaniṣadam abrūmeti |
4.21.d: उपनिषदम् भो ब्रूहीति उक्ता त उपनिषत् ब्राह्मीं वाव त उपनिषदम् अब्रूमेति ।
4.21.e: " Sir, tell the upaniṣad." " The upaniṣad has been told thee. Verily, we told thee the upaniṣad of the brahman.'"

4.21.s: tasyai tapo damaḥ karmeti pratiṣṭhā vedās sarvāṅgāṇi satyam āyatanam |
4.21.d: तस्यै तपो दमः कर्मेति प्रतिष्ठा वेदास् सर्वाङ्गाणि सत्यम् आयतनम् ।
4.21.e: Penance, restraint, action are its foundation, the Vedas all its limbs, truth its abode.
4.21.m: Austerity, self-restraint, action are its foundation; the Vedas are all its limbs; truth is its abode.

4.21.s: yo vā etām evaṃ vedāpahatya pāpmānam anante svarge loke 'jyeye pratitiṣṭhati | daśame 'nuvāke caturthaḥ khaṇḍaḥ | daśamo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
4.21.d: यो वा एताम् एवं वेदापहत्य पाप्मानम् अनन्ते स्वर्गे लोके ऽज्येये प्रतितिष्ठति । दशमे ऽनुवाके चतुर्थः खण्डः । दशमो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
4.21.e: Verily he who knows this \upaniṣad'\ thus, having smitten away evil, stands firm in the endless heavenly world that is not to be injured.
4.21.m:
He who indeed knows this thus, striking off evil, is established in the endless, unconquerable heavenly world—he is established.
The fourth khaṇḍa in the tenth anuvāka.
The tenth anuvāka is completed.

4.22.s: āśā vā idam agra āsīd bhaviṣyad eva tad abhavat tā āpo 'bhavan |
4.22.d: आशा वा इदम् अग्र आसीद् भविष्यद् एव तद् अभवत् ता आपो ऽभवन् ।
4.22.e: Verily this was in the beginning space, being about to become. It became. It became the waters.
4.22.m:
Space (hope) indeed was here in the beginning, just about to become.
That became.
That became the waters.

4.22.s: tās tapo 'tapyanta tās tapas tepānā huss ity eva prācīḥ prāśvasan sa vāva prāṇo 'bhavat |
4.22.d: तास् तपो ऽतप्यन्त तास् तपस् तेपाना हुस्स् इत्य् एव प्राचीः प्राश्वसन् स वाव प्राणो ऽभवत् ।
4.22.e: They performed penance. Having performed penance [uttering] huss, they breathed forth forward. That became breath.
4.22.m:
They practiced austerity.
As they practiced austerity, they breathed forward with the sound "huss!".
That indeed became the forward-breath (prāṇa).

4.22.d: ताः प्राण्यापानन् स वा अपानो ऽभवत् ।
4.22.e: Having breathed forth, they breathed out. That became exhalation.
4.22.m:
Having breathed forward, they breathed downward.
That indeed became the downward-breath (apāna).

4.22.s: tā apānya vyānan sa vāva vyāno 'bhavat |
4.22.d: ता अपान्य व्यानन् स वाव व्यानो ऽभवत् ।
4.22.e: Having breathed out, they breathed asunder. That became the vydna.
4.22.m:
Having breathed downward, they breathed dispersed.
That indeed became the dispersed-breath (vyāna).

4.22.s: tā vyānya samānan sa vāva samāno 'bhavat |
4.22.d: ता व्यान्य समानन् स वाव समानो ऽभवत् ।
4.22.e: Having breathed asunder, they breathed together. That became the samdna.
4.22.m:
Having breathed dispersed, they breathed together.
That indeed became the equalized-breath (samāna).

4.22.d: तास् समान्योदानन् स वा उदानो ऽभवत् ।
4.22.e: Having breathed together, they breathed up. That became the uddna.
4.22.m:
Having breathed together, they breathed upward.
That indeed became the upward-breath (udāna).

4.22.s: tad idam ekam eva sadhamādyam āsīd aviviktam |
4.22.d: तद् इदम् एकम् एव सधमाद्यम् आसीद् अविविक्तम् ।
4.22.e: This [all] was one, associated, not distinguished.
4.22.m: This was then just one united whole, undistinguished.

4.22.s: sa nāmarūpam akuruta tenainad vyavinak vi ha pāpmano vicyate ya evaṃ veda |
4.22.d: स नामरूपम् अकुरुत तेनैनद् व्यविनक् वि ह पाप्मनो विच्यते य एवं वेद ।
4.22.e: He made name and form. Thereby he distinguished it. Distinguished from evil is he who knows thus.
4.22.m:
He made name and form.
By that he distinguished it.
He who knows thus is indeed separated from evil.

4.22.s: tad asau vā ādityaḥ prāṇo 'gnir apāna āpo vyāno diśas samānaś candramā udānaḥ |
4.22.d: तद् असौ वा आदित्यः प्राणो ऽग्निर् अपान आपो व्यानो दिशस् समानश् चन्द्रमा उदानः ।
4.22.e: Verily yonder sun is breath, Agni is exhalation, the waters are the vydna, the quarters are the samdna, the moon is the uddna.
4.22.m: Now that sun over there is the forward-breath; Agni is the downward-breath; the waters are the dispersed-breath; the directions are the equalized-breath; the moon is the upward-breath.

4.22.s: tad vā etad ekam abhavat prāṇa eva sa ya evam etad ekam bhavad vedaivaṃ haitad ekadhā bhavatīty ekadhaiva śreṣṭhas svānām bhavati |
4.22.d: तद् वा एतद् एकम् अभवत् प्राण एव स य एवम् एतद् एकम् भवद् वेदैवं हैतद् एकधा भवतीत्य् एकधैव श्रेष्ठस् स्वानाम् भवति ।
4.22.e: Verily that became one, viz. breath. He who thus knows this as becoming one [saying]: " Verily this thus becometh onefold," he becomes at once the first among his own people,
4.22.m:
That indeed became one: breath alone.
He who knows this thus becoming one—that this becomes singly unified—becomes the foremost of his own [people] in a single manner.

4.22.s: tad agnir vai prāṇo vāg iti pṛthivī vāyur vai prāṇo vāg ity antarikṣam ādityo vai prāṇo vāg iti dyaur diśo vai prāṇo vāg iti śrotraṃ candramā vai prāṇo vāg iti manaḥ pumān vai prāṇo vāg iti strī |
4.22.d: तद् अग्निर् वै प्राणो वाग् इति पृथिवी वायुर् वै प्राणो वाग् इत्य् अन्तरिक्षम् आदित्यो वै प्राणो वाग् इति द्यौर् दिशो वै प्राणो वाग् इति श्रोत्रं चन्द्रमा वै प्राणो वाग् इति मनः पुमान् वै प्राणो वाग् इति स्त्री ।
4.22.e: Verily now Agni is breath, speech is the earth; Vayu is breath, speech is the atmosphere; the sun is breath, speech is the sky; the quarters are breath, speech is hearing; the moon is breath, speech is mind; man is breath, speech is woman.
4.22.m: So Agni is breath, earth is speech; Vāyu is breath, the intermediate space is speech; Āditya is breath, heaven is speech; the directions are breath, the ear is speech; the moon is breath, the mind is speech; the male is breath, the female is speech.

4.22.s: tasyedaṃ sṛṣṭaṃ śithilam bhuvanam āsīd aparyāptam |
4.22.d: तस्येदं सृष्टं शिथिलम् भुवनम् आसीद् अपर्याप्तम् ।
4.22.e: That creation of his, when created, was unsteady, not fully completed.
4.22.m: This creation of his was a loose, unstable world, inadequate.

4.22.s: sa manorūpam akuruta tena tat paryāpnot dṛḍhaṃ ha vā asyedaṃ sṛṣṭam aśithilam bhuvanam paryāptam bhavati ya evaṃ veda | ekādaśe 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
4.22.d: स मनोरूपम् अकुरुत तेन तत् पर्याप्नोत् दृढं ह वा अस्येदं सृष्टम् अशिथिलम् भुवनम् पर्याप्तम् भवति य एवं वेद । एकादशे ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
4.22.e: He made the form of mind. By it he completed it. Verily stable becomes this creation which was created, not unsteady, completed, for him who knows thus.
4.22.m: He made the form of mind; with it he encompassed it. Firm indeed, not loose, adequate does this created world become for him who knows thus. / First khaṇḍa in the eleventh anuvāka.

4.23.s: saiṣā caturdhā vihitā śrīr udgīthas sāmārkyaṃ jyeṣṭhabrāhmaṇam |
4.23.d: सैषा चतुर्धा विहिता श्रीर् उद्गीथस् सामार्क्यं ज्येष्ठब्राह्मणम् ।
4.23.e: This is the fortune divided into four parts, viz. the udgītha, the sāman, the arkya, the chief brāhmaṇa.
4.23.m: This is that prosperity, arranged in four ways: the udgītha, the sāman, the ṛc-nature (arkya), and the supreme brāhmaṇa.

4.23.s: prāṇo vāvod vāg gī sa udgīthaḥ |
4.23.d: प्राणो वावोद् वाग् गी स उद्गीथः ।
4.23.e: Verily breath is ud, speech is gl/ that is the udgītha.
4.23.m: Breath indeed is ud; speech is gī: that is the udgītha.

4.23.s: prāṇo vāvāmo vāk sā tat sāma |
4.23.d: प्राणो वावामो वाक् सा तत् साम ।
4.23.e: Verily breath is he (ama), speech is she (sd); that is the sāman.
4.23.m: Breath indeed is ama; speech is sā: that is the sāman.

4.23.s: prāṇo vāva ko vāg ṛk tad arkyam |
4.23.d: प्राणो वाव को वाग् ऋक् तद् अर्क्यम् ।
4.23.e: Verily breath is ka, speech is rk; that is the arkya.
4.23.m: Breath indeed is ka; speech is ṛk: that is the arkya.

4.23.s: prāṇo vāva jyeṣṭho vāg brāhmaṇaṃ taj jyeṣṭhabrāhmaṇam |
4.23.d: प्राणो वाव ज्येष्ठो वाग् ब्राह्मणं तज् ज्येष्ठब्राह्मणम् ।
4.23.e: Verily breath is the highest, speech is the brāhmaṇa; that is the highest been told thee, since the elements have been told thee. With three elements separately (?) verily we told thee the upaniṣad."
4.23.m: Breath indeed is the eldest; speech is the brāhmaṇa. That is the eldest brāhmaṇa.

4.23.s: upaniṣadam bho brūhīti uktā ta upaniṣad yasya te dhātava uktāḥ tridhātu viṣu vāva ta upaniṣadam abrūmeti |
4.23.d: उपनिषदम् भो ब्रूहीति उक्ता त उपनिषद् यस्य ते धातव उक्ताः त्रिधातु विषु वाव त उपनिषदम् अब्रूमेति ।
4.23.m:
‘Sir, teach the upaniṣad!’
‘The upaniṣad has been taught to you whose elements have been taught.
It was indeed the three-element [composition] in various ways that we taught you as the upaniṣad.’

4.23.s: etac chuklaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ tāmraṃ sāmavarṇa iti ha smāha yadaiva śuklakṛṣṇe tāmro varṇo 'bhyavaiti sa vai te vṛṅte daśama mānuṣam iti tridhātu sa aikṣata kva nu ma uttānāya śayānāyemā devatā baliṃ hareyur iti | ekādaśe 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
4.23.d: एतच् छुक्लं कृष्णं ताम्रं सामवर्ण इति ह स्माह यदैव शुक्लकृष्णे ताम्रो वर्णो ऽभ्यवैति स वै ते वृङ्ते दशम मानुषम् इति त्रिधातु स ऐक्षत क्व नु म उत्तानाय शयानायेमा देवता बलिं हरेयुर् इति । एकादशे ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः ।
4.23.e: " That white, black, copper-red is the color of the sāman," he used to say; " when the copper-red color descendeth into the white and black, it snatcheth these two unto itself." He considered: "Where now may these divinities bring tribute to me lying supine?"
4.23.m:
‘This white, dark, [and] copper-colored [form] is the color of the sāman,’ he used to say. ‘Whenever the copper color enters into the white and dark, that indeed wards off your tenth, human [state]’—this is the three-element [composition].
He reflected: ‘Where now may these deities bring tribute to me as I lie stretched out?’
Second khaṇḍa in the eleventh anuvāka.

4.24.e: He chose man for a resort,
4.24.m: He chose the person itself for entering.

4.24.s: tam purastāt pratyañcam prāviśat tasmā urur abhavat tad urasa urastvam |
4.24.d: तम् पुरस्तात् प्रत्यञ्चम् प्राविशत् तस्मा उरुर् अभवत् तद् उरस उरस्त्वम् ।
4.24.e: He entered him from the front (east), turned toward him. For him he became wide (uru). Therefore the breast (toras) is called so.
4.24.m:
He entered it from the front, moving inward.
For him, it became broad (uru).
That is the chest-nature (urastva) of the chest (uras).

4.24.s: tasmā atrasada etā devatā baliṃ haranti |
4.24.d: तस्मा अत्रसद एता देवता बलिं हरन्ति ।
4.24.e: T'o him sitting there these divinities bring tribute.
4.24.m: To him, sitting here, these deities bring tribute.

4.24.s: vācam anuharantīm agnir asmai baliṃ harati |
4.24.d: वाचम् अनुहरन्तीम् अग्निर् अस्मै बलिं हरति ।
4.24.e: Agni brings to him as tribute speech bringing after.
4.24.m: Following speech, Agni brings tribute to him.

4.24.d: मनो ऽनुहरच् चन्द्रमा अस्मै बलिं हरति ।
4.24.e: The moon brings to him as tribute mind bringing after.
4.24.m: Following mind, Moon brings tribute to him.

4.24.d: चक्षुर् अनुहरद् आदित्यो ऽस्मै बलिं हरति ।
4.24.e: The sun brings to him as tribute sight bringing after.
4.24.m: Following the eye, Āditya brings tribute to him.

4.24.d: श्रोत्रम् अनुहरद् दिशो ऽस्मै बलिं हरन्ति ।
4.24.e: The quarters bring to him as tribute hearing bringing after.
4.24.m: Following the ear, the directions bring tribute to him.

4.24.s: prāṇam anuharantaṃ vāyur asmai baliṃ harati |
4.24.d: प्राणम् अनुहरन्तं वायुर् अस्मै बलिं हरति ।
4.24.e: Vayu brings to him as tribute breath bringing after.
4.24.m: Following the breath, Vāyu brings tribute to him.

4.24.s: tasyaite niṣkhātāḥ panthā balivāhanā ime prāṇāḥ evaṃ haitaṃ niṣkhātāḥ panthā balivāhanās sarvato 'piyanti prāṇā ya evaṃ veda |
4.24.d: तस्यैते निष्खाताः पन्था बलिवाहना इमे प्राणाः एवं हैतं निष्खाताः पन्था बलिवाहनास् सर्वतो ऽपियन्ति प्राणा य एवं वेद ।
4.24.e: These are his dug-out paths, carrying tribute, [viz.] these breaths. Thus dug-out paths, carrying tribute, approach from all sides him who knows thus.
4.24.m:
These dug-out paths of his are tribute-bearers, these vital breaths.
In this way, dug-out paths, tribute-bearers, vital breaths come together from all sides to him who knows thus.

4.24.s: sā haiṣā brahmāsandīm ārūḍhā ā hāsmai brahmāsandīṃ haranty adhi ha brahmāsandīṃ rohati ya evaṃ veda |
4.24.d: सा हैषा ब्रह्मासन्दीम् आरूढा आ हास्मै ब्रह्मासन्दीं हरन्त्य् अधि ह ब्रह्मासन्दीं रोहति य एवं वेद ।
4.24.e: That [divinity] is seated on the brahman-throne. Unto him they bring the brahman-throne, he mounts the brahman-throne, who knows thus.
4.24.m:
That indeed has mounted the brahman-chair.
They bring the brahman-chair to him, and he mounts the brahman-chair, who knows thus.

4.24.s: tad etad brahmayaśaś śriyā parivṛḍham brahma ha tu san yaśasā śriyā parivṛḍho bhavati ya evaṃ veda |
4.24.d: तद् एतद् ब्रह्मयशश् श्रिया परिवृढम् ब्रह्म ह तु सन् यशसा श्रिया परिवृढो भवति य एवं वेद ।
4.24.e: That same brahman-glory is encompassed by fortune. But being the brahman he is encompassed by glory [and] by fortune who knows thus.
4.24.m:
That is this brahman-glory surrounded by prosperity.
Being brahman indeed, he becomes surrounded by glory and prosperity, who knows thus.

4.24.s: tasyaiṣa ādeśo yo 'yaṃ dakṣiṇe 'kṣann antaḥ tasya yac chuklaṃ tad ṛcāṃ rūpaṃ yat kṛṣṇaṃ tat sāmnāṃ yad eva tāmram iva babhrur iva tad yajuṣām |
4.24.d: तस्यैष आदेशो यो ऽयं दक्षिणे ऽक्षन्न् अन्तः तस्य यच् छुक्लं तद् ऋचां रूपं यत् कृष्णं तत् साम्नां यद् एव ताम्रम् इव बभ्रुर् इव तद् यजुषाम् ।
4.24.e: Regarding it [there is] this direction which is here in the right eye. What of it is white, that is the form of the ṛc's; what is black, that [is the form] of the sāmans; what is copper-red, as it were, brownish, as it were, that [is the form] of the yajuses.
4.24.m:
This is its instruction: that which is here within the right eye.
What is white in it is the form of the ṛcs; what is dark is that of the sāmans; what is copper-colored as it were, brownish as it were, is that of the yajuses.

4.24.s: ya evāyaṃ cakṣuṣi puruṣa eṣa indra eṣa prajāpatis samaḥ pṛthivyā sama ākāśena samo divā samas sarveṇa bhūtena eṣa paro divo dīpyate eṣa evedaṃ sarvam ity upāsitavyam | ekādaśe 'nuvāke tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
4.24.d: य एवायं चक्षुषि पुरुष एष इन्द्र एष प्रजापतिस् समः पृथिव्या सम आकाशेन समो दिवा समस् सर्वेण भूतेन एष परो दिवो दीप्यते एष एवेदं सर्वम् इत्य् उपासितव्यम् । एकादशे ऽनुवाके तृतीयः खण्डः ।
4.24.e: What this person in the eye is, that is Indra, that is Prajapati, the same with the earth, the same with space, the same with the sky, the same with all existence; he shines beyond the sky. One should worship him [saying]: " He is this all."
4.24.m:
The person that is here in the eye—this is Indra, this is Prajāpati; equal to the earth, equal to the intermediate space, equal to heaven, equal to all being.
This shines beyond heaven.
It should be meditated upon as: ‘This alone is everything.’
Third khaṇḍa in the eleventh anuvāka.

4.25.s: sac cāsac cāsac ca sac ca vāk ca manaś ca vāk ca cakṣuś ca śrotraṃ ca śrotraṃ ca cakṣuś ca śraddhā ca tapaś ca tapaś ca śraddhā ca tāni ṣoḍaśa |
4.25.d: सच् चासच् चासच् च सच् च वाक् च मनश् च वाक् च चक्षुश् च श्रोत्रं च श्रोत्रं च चक्षुश् च श्रद्धा च तपश् च तपश् च श्रद्धा च तानि षोडश ।
4.25.m: The real and the unreal, and the unreal and the real; and speech and mind, and [mind and] speech; and the eye and the ear, and the ear and the eye; and faith and ascetic heat, and ascetic heat and faith: these are sixteen.

4.25.s: ṣoḍaśakalam brahma sa ya evam etat ṣoḍaśakalam brahma veda tam evaitat ṣoḍaśakalam brahmāpyeti |
4.25.d: षोडशकलम् ब्रह्म स य एवम् एतत् षोडशकलम् ब्रह्म वेद तम् एवैतत् षोडशकलम् ब्रह्माप्येति ।
4.25.e: Being and non-being, non-being and being, speech and mind, [mind and] speech, sight and hearing, hearing and sight, faith and penance, penance and faith: these are sixteen. 4. Sixteenfold is the brahman. He who thus knows this sixteenfold brahman, him this sixteenfold brahman comes unto.
4.25.m:
Brahman has sixteen parts.
Whoever knows this sixteen-part brahman thus, to him this sixteen-part brahman merges.

4.25.s: vedo brahma tasya satyam āyatanaṃ śamaḥ pratiṣṭhā damaś ca |
4.25.d: वेदो ब्रह्म तस्य सत्यम् आयतनं शमः प्रतिष्ठा दमश् च ।
4.25.e: The Veda is the brahman, truth is its abode, tranquillity and restraint its foundation.
4.25.m: Brahman is known. Truth is its abode, quietude its firm foundation, and self-restraint.

4.25.s: tad yathā śvaḥ praiṣyan pāpāt karmaṇo jugupsetaivam evāhar-ahaḥ pāpāt karmaṇo jugupsetākālāt |
4.25.d: तद् यथा श्वः प्रैष्यन् पापात् कर्मणो जुगुप्सेतैवम् एवाहर्-अहः पापात् कर्मणो जुगुप्सेताकालात् ।
4.25.e: As one about to decease the next day would guard himself against an evil action, even so he should day by day guard against an evil action, until the time.
4.25.m: Then just as one who is about to depart tomorrow would shrink from an evil deed, so day by day he should shrink from an evil deed until the end of his time.

4.25.e: Now of these the virdj is ten-footed.
4.25.m: Now this ten-footed virāj of theirs.

4.25.s: daśa puruṣe svarganarakāṇi tāny enaṃ svargaṃ gatāni svargaṃ gamayanti narakaṃ gatāni narakaṃ gamayanti | ekādaśe 'nuvāke caturthaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
4.25.d: दश पुरुषे स्वर्गनरकाणि तान्य् एनं स्वर्गं गतानि स्वर्गं गमयन्ति नरकं गतानि नरकं गमयन्ति । एकादशे ऽनुवाके चतुर्थः खण्डः ।
4.25.e: There are ten heavens and hells in man. They, having gone to heaven, cause him to go to heaven; having gone to hell, they cause him to go to hell.
4.25.m:
There are ten heavens and hells in the person.
Going to heaven, they make him go to heaven; going to hell, they make him go to hell.
Fourth khaṇḍa in the eleventh anuvāka.

4.26.s: mano narako vāṅ narakaḥ prāṇo narakaś cakṣur narakaś śrotraṃ narakas tvaṅ narako hastau narako gudaṃ narakaś śiśnaṃ narakaḥ pādau narakaḥ |
4.26.d: मनो नरको वाङ् नरकः प्राणो नरकश् चक्षुर् नरकश् श्रोत्रं नरकस् त्वङ् नरको हस्तौ नरको गुदं नरकश् शिश्नं नरकः पादौ नरकः ।
4.26.e: Mind is a hell, speech is a hell, breath is a hell, sight is a hell, heai-ing is a hell, the skin is a hell, both hands are a hell, the rectum is a hell, the penis is a hell, both feet are a hell.
4.26.m: Mind is a hell; speech is a hell; breath is a hell; the eye is a hell; the ear is a hell; the skin is a hell; the two hands are a hell; the rectum is a hell; the penis is a hell; the two feet are a hell.

4.26.e: He knows: " With the mind I know those things which are to be examined."
4.26.m: ‘With the mind I know things to be investigated’—thus he knows.

4.26.e: He knows: " With speech I know savors."
4.26.m: ‘With speech I know tastes’—thus he knows.

4.26.e: He knows: " With breath I know odors." 34. " -ur. 35. ' -af. 36. ' -ksa-. '' vad-.
4.26.m: ‘With breath I know odors’—thus he knows.

4.26.e: He knows: " With sight I know forms."
4.26.m: ‘With the eye I know forms’—thus he knows.

4.26.e: He knows: "With hearing I know sounds."
4.26.m: ‘With the ear I know sounds’—thus he knows.

4.26.e: He knows: "With the skin I know contacts."
4.26.m: ‘With the skin I know sensations of touch’—thus he knows.

4.26.e: He knows: "With both hands I know works."
4.26.m: ‘With the two hands I know actions’—thus he knows.

4.26.e: He knows: " With the belly I know hunger."
4.26.m: ‘With the belly I know hunger’—thus he knows.

4.26.e: He knows: "With the penis I know delights."
4.26.m: ‘With the penis I know pleasures’—thus he knows.

4.26.e: He knows: "With both feet I know roads."
4.26.m: ‘With the two feet I know paths’—thus he knows.

4.26.s: plakṣasya prāsravaṇasya prādeśamātrād udak tat pṛthivyai madhyam atha yatraite sapta rṣayas tad divo madhyam |
4.26.d: प्लक्षस्य प्रास्रवणस्य प्रादेशमात्राद् उदक् तत् पृथिव्यै मध्यम् अथ यत्रैते सप्त र्षयस् तद् दिवो मध्यम् ।
4.26.e: Just one span to the north of the Plaksa Prasravana is the middle of the earth. And where these seven sages ( Ursa major) are, that is the middle of the sky.
4.26.m:
A span’s length north of Plakṣa Prāsravaṇa: that is the center of the earth.
Now where these Seven Seers are: that is the center of heaven.

4.26.s: atha yatraita ūṣās tat pṛthivyai hṛdayam atha yad etat kṛṣṇaṃ candramasi tad divo hṛdayam |
4.26.d: अथ यत्रैत ऊषास् तत् पृथिव्यै हृदयम् अथ यद् एतत् कृष्णं चन्द्रमसि तद् दिवो हृदयम् ।
4.26.e: And where these salts are, that is the heart of the earth. And what is black in the moon, that is the heart of the sky.
4.26.m:
Now where these saline tracts are: that is the heart of the earth.
Now that which is dark in the Moon: that is the heart of heaven.

4.26.s: sa ya evam ete dyāvāpṛthivyor madhye ca hṛdaye ca veda nākāmo 'smāl lokāt praiti |
4.26.d: स य एवम् एते द्यावापृथिव्योर् मध्ये च हृदये च वेद नाकामो ऽस्माल् लोकात् प्रैति ।
4.26.e: He who thus knows the two centers and the two hearts of the sky and the earth departs not unwilling from this world.
4.26.m: Whoever knows these two centers and two hearts of heaven and earth thus, does not depart from this world unsatisfied.

4.26.s: namo 'tisāmāyaituretāya dhṛtarāṣṭrāya pārthuśravasāya ye ca prāṇaṃ rakṣanti te mā rakṣantu svasti karmeti gārhapatyaś śama ity āhavanīyo dama ity anvāhāryapacanaḥ | ekādaśe 'nuvāke pañcamaḥ khaḥḍaḥ | ekādaśo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
4.26.d: नमो ऽतिसामायैतुरेताय धृतराष्ट्राय पार्थुश्रवसाय ये च प्राणं रक्षन्ति ते मा रक्षन्तु स्वस्ति कर्मेति गार्हपत्यश् शम इत्य् आहवनीयो दम इत्य् अन्वाहार्यपचनः । एकादशे ऽनुवाके पञ्चमः खःडः । एकादशो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
4.26.e: Homage to Atisama Etureta (?), to Dhrtarastra, to Parthu9ravasa, and let those who protect breath protect me. Hail. 'Action' is the householder's fire; 'tranquillity' is the dhavamya fire; 'selfrostraint' is the anvdhdryapacana fire.
4.26.m:
Homage to the transcendent sāman, to Aitureta, to Dhṛtarāṣṭra Pārthuśravasa! And those who guard the breath, let them guard me!
Well-being!
‘Action’—such is the Gārhapatya; ‘quietude’—such is the Āhavanīya; ‘self-restraint’—such is the Anvāhāryapacana.
Fifth khaṇḍa in the eleventh anuvāka.
The eleventh anuvāka is completed.

4.27.s: kā sāvitrī agnir eva savitā pṛthivī sāvitrī |
4.27.d: का सावित्री अग्निर् एव सविता पृथिवी सावित्री ।
4.27.e: What is Savitar? What is Savitri? Agni is Savitar, earth Savitri.

4.27.s: sa yatrāgnis tat pṛthivī yatra vā pṛthivī tad agniḥ te dve yonī tad ekam mithunam |
4.27.d: स यत्राग्निस् तत् पृथिवी यत्र वा पृथिवी तद् अग्निः ते द्वे योनी तद् एकम् मिथुनम् ।
4.27.e: Where Agni is, there is earth; or where earth is, there is Agni. These are two wombs. This is one couple.

4.27.s: kas savitā kā sāvitrī varuṇa eva savitā āpas sāvitrī |
4.27.d: कस् सविता का सावित्री वरुण एव सविता आपस् सावित्री ।
4.27.e: What is Savitar? What is Savitri? Varuna is Savitar, the waters are Savitri.
4.27.m:
Who is Savitṛ?
Who is the Sāvitrī?
Varuṇa is Savitṛ;
the waters are the Sāvitrī.

4.27.s: sa yatra varuṇas tad āpo yatra vāpas tad varuṇaḥ te dve yonī
4.27.d: स यत्र वरुणस् तद् आपो यत्र वापस् तद् वरुणः ते द्वे योनी
4.27.e: Where Varuna is, there the waters are; or where the waters are, there is Varuna. These are two wombs. [This is one couple.]

4.27.s: kas savitā kā sāvitrī vāyur eva savitā ākāśas sāvitrī |
4.27.d: कस् सविता का सावित्री वायुर् एव सविता आकाशस् सावित्री ।
4.27.e: What is Savitar? What is Savitri? Vfiyu is Savitar, space Savitri.
4.27.m:
Who is Savitṛ?
Who is the Sāvitrī?
Vāyu is Savitṛ;
space is the Sāvitrī.

4.27.s: sa yatra vāyus tad ākāśo yatra vākāśas tad vāyuḥ te dve yonī tad ekam mithunam |
4.27.d: स यत्र वायुस् तद् आकाशो यत्र वाकाशस् तद् वायुः ते द्वे योनी तद् एकम् मिथुनम् ।
4.27.e: Where Vayu is, there is space; or where space is, there is Vayu. These are two wombs. This is one couple.

4.27.s: kas savitā kā sāvitrī yajña eva savitā chandāṃsi sāvitrī |
4.27.d: कस् सविता का सावित्री यज्ञ एव सविता छन्दांसि सावित्री ।
4.27.e: What is Savitar? What is Savitri? The sacrifice is Savitar, the metres are Savitri.
4.27.m:
Who is Savitṛ?
Who is the Sāvitrī?
The sacrifice is Savitṛ;
the metres are the Sāvitrī.

4.27.s: sa yatra yajñas tac chandāṃsi yatra vā chandāṃsi tad yajñaḥ te dve yonī tad ekam mithunam |
4.27.d: स यत्र यज्ञस् तच् छन्दांसि यत्र वा छन्दांसि तद् यज्ञः ते द्वे योनी तद् एकम् मिथुनम् ।
4.27.e: Where the sacrifice is, there the metres are; or where the metres are, there is the sacrifice. These are two wombs. This is one couple.

4.27.s: kas savitā kā sāvitrī stanayitnur eva savitā vidyut sāvitrī |
4.27.d: कस् सविता का सावित्री स्तनयित्नुर् एव सविता विद्युत् सावित्री ।
4.27.e: What is Savitar? What is Savitri? Thunder is Savitar, lightning Savitri.
4.27.m:
Who is Savitṛ?
Who is the Sāvitrī?
The thunder-cloud is Savitṛ;
lightning is the Sāvitrī.

4.27.s: sa yatra stanayitnus tad vidyud yatra vā vidyut tat stanayitnuḥ te dve yonī tad ekam mithunam |
4.27.d: स यत्र स्तनयित्नुस् तद् विद्युद् यत्र वा विद्युत् तत् स्तनयित्नुः ते द्वे योनी तद् एकम् मिथुनम् ।
4.27.e: Where thunder is, there is lightning; or where lightning is, there is thunder. These are two wombs. This is one couple.

4.27.s: kas savitā kā sāvitrī āditya eva savitā dyaus sāvitrī |
4.27.d: कस् सविता का सावित्री आदित्य एव सविता द्यौस् सावित्री ।
4.27.e: What is Savitar? What is Savitri? The sun is Savitar, the sky Savitri.
4.27.m:
Who is Savitṛ?
Who is the Sāvitrī?
Āditya is Savitṛ;
heaven is the Sāvitrī.

4.27.s: sa yatrādityas tad dyaur yatra vā dyaus tad ādityaḥ te dve yonī tad ekam mithunam |
4.27.d: स यत्रादित्यस् तद् द्यौर् यत्र वा द्यौस् तद् आदित्यः ते द्वे योनी तद् एकम् मिथुनम् ।
4.27.e: Where the sun is, there is the sky; or where the sky is, there is the sun. These are two wombs. This is one couple,

4.27.s: kas savitā kā sāvitrī candra eva savitā nakṣatrāṇi sāvitrī |
4.27.d: कस् सविता का सावित्री चन्द्र एव सविता नक्षत्राणि सावित्री ।
4.27.e: What is Savitar? What is Savitri? The moon is Savitar, the asterisms are Savitri.
4.27.m:
Who is Savitṛ?
Who is the Sāvitrī?
The moon is Savitṛ;
the lunar mansions are the Sāvitrī.

4.27.s: sa yatra candras tan nakṣatrāṇi yatra vā nakṣatrāṇi tac candraḥ te dve yonī tad ekam mithunam |
4.27.d: स यत्र चन्द्रस् तन् नक्षत्राणि यत्र वा नक्षत्राणि तच् चन्द्रः ते द्वे योनी तद् एकम् मिथुनम् ।
4.27.e: Where the moon is, there the asterisms are; or where the asterisms are, there is the moon. These are two wombs. This is one couple.

4.27.s: kas savitā kā sāvitrī mana eva savitā vāk sāvitrī |
4.27.d: कस् सविता का सावित्री मन एव सविता वाक् सावित्री ।
4.27.e: What is Savitar? What is Savitri? Mind is Savitar, speech is Savitri.
4.27.m:
Who is Savitṛ?
Who is the Sāvitrī?
Mind is Savitṛ;
speech is the Sāvitrī.

4.27.s: sa yatra manas tad vāg yatra vāk tan manaḥ te dve yonī tad ekam mithunam |
4.27.d: स यत्र मनस् तद् वाग् यत्र वाक् तन् मनः ते द्वे योनी तद् एकम् मिथुनम् ।
4.27.e: Where mind is, there is speech; or where speech is, there is mind. These are two wombs. This is one couple, n. What is Savitar? What is Savitri? Man is Savitar, woman Savitri. Where man is, there is woman; or where woman is, there is man. These are two wombs. This is one couple.

4.27.s: kas savitā kā sāvitrī puruṣa savitā strī sāvitrī sa yatra puruṣas tat strī yatra vā strī tat puruṣaḥ te dve yonī tad ekam mithunam | dvādaśe 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
4.27.d: कस् सविता का सावित्री पुरुष सविता स्त्री सावित्री स यत्र पुरुषस् तत् स्त्री यत्र वा स्त्री तत् पुरुषः ते द्वे योनी तद् एकम् मिथुनम् । द्वादशे ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
4.27.e: 'i)-. ' abbreviate here and in the following. »B.-ttn. *~lh{\).
4.27.m:
Who is Savitṛ?
Who is Sāvitrī?
Man [alone] is Savitṛ,
woman is Sāvitrī.
Where there is man, there is woman; or where there is woman, there is man.
These are two wombs,
that is one pair.
First khaṇḍa in the twelfth anuvāka.

4.28.s: tasyā eṣa prathamaḥ pādo bhūs tat savitur vareṇyam iti agnir vai vareṇyam āpo vai vareṇyam candramā vai vareṇyam |
4.28.d: तस्या एष प्रथमः पादो भूस् तत् सवितुर् वरेण्यम् इति अग्निर् वै वरेण्यम् आपो वै वरेण्यम् चन्द्रमा वै वरेण्यम् ।
4.28.e: This is its first pāda: "Bhus; that desirable [splendor] of Savitar." Fire indeed is what is desirable. Waters indeed are what is desirable. The moon indeed is what is desirable.

4.28.s: tasyā eṣa dvitīyaḥ pādo bhargamayo bhuvo bhargo devasya dhīmahīti agnir vai bhargaḥ ādityo vai bhargaḥ candramā vai bhargaḥ |
4.28.d: तस्या एष द्वितीयः पादो भर्गमयो भुवो भर्गो देवस्य धीमहीति अग्निर् वै भर्गः आदित्यो वै भर्गः चन्द्रमा वै भर्गः ।
4.28.e: This is its second pāda, made up of splendor: "Bhuvas; may we obtain the god's splendor." Fire indeed is splendor. The sun indeed is splendor. The moon indeed is splendor, a.

4.28.s: tasyā eṣa tṛtīyaḥ pādas svar dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayād iti yajño vai pracodayati strī ca vai puruṣaś ca prajanayataḥ |
4.28.d: तस्या एष तृतीयः पादस् स्वर् धियो यो नः प्रचोदयाद् इति यज्ञो वै प्रचोदयति स्त्री च वै पुरुषश् च प्रजनयतः ।
4.28.e: This is its third pāda: "Svar; who may impel our devotion." The sacrifice indeed impels. Woman and man propagate.

4.28.s: bhūr bhuvas tat savitur vareṇyam bhargo devasya dhīmahīti agnir vai bhargaḥ ādityo vai bhargaḥ candramā vai bhargaḥ |
4.28.d: भूर् भुवस् तत् सवितुर् वरेण्यम् भर्गो देवस्य धीमहीति अग्निर् वै भर्गः आदित्यो वै भर्गः चन्द्रमा वै भर्गः ।
4.28.e: " Bhus, bhuvas; may we obtain that desirable splendor of god Savitar." Agni is splendor. The Sun is splendor. The Moon is splendor.

4.28.s: svar dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayād iti yajño vai pracodayati strī ca vai puruṣaś ca prajanayataḥ |
4.28.d: स्वर् धियो यो नः प्रचोदयाद् इति यज्ञो वै प्रचोदयति स्त्री च वै पुरुषश् च प्रजनयतः ।
4.28.e: "Svar; who shall impel our devotion." The sacrifice impels. Woman and man propagate.

4.28.s: bhūr bhuvas svas tat savitur vareṇyam bhargo devasya dhīmahi dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayād iti yo vā etāṃ sāvitrīm evaṃ vedāpa punarmṛtyuṃ tarati sāvitryā eva salokatāṃ jayati sāvitryā eva salokatāṃ jayati | dvādaśe 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ | dvādaśo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
4.28.d: भूर् भुवस् स्वस् तत् सवितुर् वरेण्यम् भर्गो देवस्य धीमहि धियो यो नः प्रचोदयाद् इति यो वा एतां सावित्रीम् एवं वेदाप पुनर्मृत्युं तरति सावित्र्या एव सलोकतां जयति सावित्र्या एव सलोकतां जयति । द्वादशे ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः । द्वादशो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
4.28.e: Bhus, bhuvas, svar; may we obtain that desirable splendor of god Savitar, who may impel our devotion." He who knows this Savitri thus overcomes second death, he wins the same world with the Sfivitri itself; he wins the same world with the Sfivitri itself.
4.28.m:
‘bhūr bhuvas svaḥ, that desirable [splendour] of Savitṛ, let us meditate on the radiance of the god, who shall impel our thoughts’.
Whoever indeed knows this Sāvitrī thus crosses beyond repeated death; he wins sharing the same world with Sāvitrī, he wins sharing the same world with Sāvitrī.
Second khaṇḍa in the twelfth anuvāka.
The twelfth anuvāka is completed.
Thus ends the Upaniṣadbrāhmaṇa.
